However, the market subsequently recovered, with the benchmark touching an intraday high of 166,989.76 points and a low of 165,585.42 points before settling in positive territory.

The market's positive close came amid a more than 4% decline in global oil prices, as renewed hopes of diplomatic progress towards ending the US-Israeli war on Iran eased concerns over energy costs and pressure on Pakistan's import bill.

Oil prices fell on Monday after Iranian and Qatari officials held a third consecutive day of talks aimed at ending the conflict, raising hopes of easing disruptions to Middle Eastern energy supplies. The absence of any meaningful military escalation over the weekend further supported sentiment in international markets.

According to Arif Habib Limited (AHL), PSX made a flat start to the week with the KSE-100 trading on both sides of the tape.

Some 41 shares rose while 58 fell with Mari Energies (+3.15%), Fauji Fertiliser (+0.92%) and Engro Holdings (+1.57%) contributing the most to index gains. Conversely, Attock Refinery (-10.0%), Oil & Gas Development Company (-1.66%) and Pakistan State Oil (-2.33%) were the biggest index drags.

Meanwhile, all refineries traded down to lower limits as the government has shifted the impact of higher petrol (MS) import costs onto local refineries to avoid passing it on to consumers, as per the October 31 pricing notification. The ex-refinery MS price rises Rs15.13 a litre to Rs282.26 per litre, but this is fully offset by a Rs14.71 per litre reduction in petroleum levy (PL) collected through refineries and a Rs0.42 per litre lower IFEM, leaving the ex-depot price unchanged at Rs377.91 a litre. “With local refineries accounting for 30% of MS supply, we estimate a burden of Rs9.4 billion/month pre-tax (Rs5.9 billion post-tax) on the sector, excluding PARCO. The measure applies for 30 days; we assume the impact for one month (Nov) only,” it wrote.

Meanwhile, October CPI rose 9.6% year-on-year (YoY) as pressures remain a concern, with inflation still above the State Bank of Pakistan’s (SBP) 5-7% target range with energy costs elevated due to the Middle East conflict. Resistance at 167.5-168k is the key level to watch over the coming sessions, AHL said.

headline: China's Xi says Middle East should not become battleground for great power rivalry
description: Visit is the first by ‌an Omani ⁠head of state since the countries established ties in 1978
author: Reuters
article_text:
The Middle East and Gulf region should not become ​a battleground for great-power rivalry, and China is willing to work with Arab nations to achieve lasting peace, Chinese ‌President Xi Jinping told Oman's sultan on Monday.

China has traditionally played a low-key diplomatic role in the Middle East, but has stepped up efforts to try to help end tensions amid the US-Israeli war on Iran, which has snarled the Strait of Hormuz and driven up global energy and shipping costs.

Xi told Omani Sultan Haitham ​bin Tariq al-Said that the world was undergoing profound changes.

"The Middle East Gulf region should not become an arena for ​great-power rivalry and geopolitical conflict. Peace and stability in the region require joint nurturing and protection by all ⁠parties," Xi said, according to China's Foreign Ministry.

China has consistently been committed to stopping the war, and hopes to contribute "wisdom and solutions to ​resolving the region's security dilemmas," he added.

China is willing to strengthen communication and coordination with Arab countries, including the Gulf Cooperation Council states, ​to work together toward restoring peace and achieving lasting stability and security, Xi said.

In a 20-point joint statement, both sides said they agree that normal and safe navigation should resume in the Strait of Hormuz. The countries also called on the US and Iran to pursue peaceful options, return to the June agreement aimed at ending the conflict, and restart dialogue.

China's Foreign Ministry said later on Monday that Zhai Jun, its special envoy to ​the Middle East, would visit Iran, Oman and Saudi Arabia this month.

First China trip

Haitham arrived in Beijing on Sunday for a two-day visit, the first by ‌an Omani ⁠head of state since the countries established ties in 1978.

Haitham told Xi his government had deep appreciation for China's positions on key issues concerning the region, Omani state media reported.

"We believe that development and stability are inextricably linked," he said.

"The prosperity of nations requires an environment defined by security, peace, respect for state sovereignty, and adherence to international law — an environment where disputes are resolved through peaceful means."

He also said ​Oman was open to entering into ​a preferential bilateral trade and ⁠investment agreement with China.

"We are confident that such an agreement would open new avenues for trade and investment, facilitate and enhance commercial and investment exchanges between our two nations," Haitham said.

China is Oman's largest trade ​partner, with tourism and business links boosted by direct flights between Beijing and Muscat since November ​last year.

Oman, which exports ⁠crude oil and energy products to China, has also been looking to further develop its renewable energy supply chains and digital commerce.

Their joint statement said the countries have agreed to deepen practical cooperation in the oil and natural gas sector, as well as expand cooperation in new energy fields ⁠such as ​solar photovoltaics, wind power, power transmission and transformation, and energy storage.

The Omani leader, who ​was welcomed on the tarmac in Beijing by People's Bank of China Governor Pan Gongsheng, also emphasised cooperation between investment and financial institutions.

The Middle East and Gulf region should not become a battleground for great-power rivalry, and China is willing to work with Arab nations to achieve lasting peace, Chinese ‌President Xi Jinping told Oman's sultan on Monday.

China has traditionally played a low-key diplomatic role in the Middle East, but has stepped up efforts to try to help end tensions amid the US-Israeli war on Iran, which has snarled the Strait of Hormuz and driven up global energy and shipping costs.

Xi told Omani Sultan Haitham bin Tariq al-Said that the world was undergoing profound changes.

"The Middle East Gulf region should not become an arena for great-power rivalry and geopolitical conflict. Peace and stability in the region require joint nurturing and protection by all ⁠parties," Xi said, according to China's Foreign Ministry.

China has consistently been committed to stopping the war, and hopes to contribute "wisdom and solutions to resolving the region's security dilemmas," he added.

China is willing to strengthen communication and coordination with Arab countries, including the Gulf Cooperation Council states, to work together toward restoring peace and achieving lasting stability and security, Xi said.

In a 20-point joint statement, both sides said they agree that normal and safe navigation should resume in the Strait of Hormuz. The countries also called on the US and Iran to pursue peaceful options, return to the June agreement aimed at ending the conflict, and restart dialogue.

China's Foreign Ministry said later on Monday that Zhai Jun, its special envoy to the Middle East, would visit Iran, Oman and Saudi Arabia this month.

First China trip

Haitham arrived in Beijing on Sunday for a two-day visit, the first by ‌an Omani ⁠head of state since the countries established ties in 1978.

Haitham told Xi his government had deep appreciation for China's positions on key issues concerning the region, Omani state media reported.

"We believe that development and stability are inextricably linked," he said.

"The prosperity of nations requires an environment defined by security, peace, respect for state sovereignty, and adherence to international law — an environment where disputes are resolved through peaceful means."

He also said Oman was open to entering into a preferential bilateral trade and ⁠investment agreement with China.

"We are confident that such an agreement would open new avenues for trade and investment, facilitate and enhance commercial and investment exchanges between our two nations," Haitham said.

China is Oman's largest trade partner, with tourism and business links boosted by direct flights between Beijing and Muscat since November last year.

Oman, which exports ⁠crude oil and energy products to China, has also been looking to further develop its renewable energy supply chains and digital commerce.

Their joint statement said the countries have agreed to deepen practical cooperation in the oil and natural gas sector, as well as expand cooperation in new energy fields ⁠such as solar photovoltaics, wind power, power transmission and transformation, and energy storage.

The Omani leader, who was welcomed on the tarmac in Beijing by People's Bank of China Governor Pan Gongsheng, also emphasised cooperation between investment and financial institutions.

text.headline.before: Peace, stability in Mideast require joint efforts, Chinese president tells Omani sultan
text.headline.after: China's Xi says Middle East should not become battleground for great power rivalry

text.cleaned_text.before:
China's President Xi Jinping on Monday called for joint efforts to maintain peace and stability in the Middle East, warning against turning the Gulf region into an arena for major-power rivalry and geopolitical conflicts, according to state media.

Xi made the remarks during talks with Oman's Sultan Haitham bin Tariq at Beijing's Great Hall of the People, Xinhua News reported.

Xi said the Middle East and the Gulf regions should "not become a wrestling ground for major-country rivalry and geopolitical conflicts, and that regional peace and stability require the joint efforts and care of all parties."

He added that China "is willing to enhance communication and coordination with Arab countries and the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries, including Oman, for the early restoration of regional peace and tranquillity and the realisation of lasting stability."

Haitham's visit marks the first by an Omani head of state since diplomatic relations between the two countries were established in 1978.

It comes amid the ongoing US-Iran conflict that began in February following US-Israeli military strikes against Tehran.

'Higher level' in bilateral ties

On the bilateral front, Xi called for further strengthening the strategic partnership with Oman to a "higher level."

"China and Oman share a longstanding friendship, which has a deep root, solid foundation, and bright prospect," Xi told Haitham.

"In recent years, the two countries enjoy ever stronger political mutual trust. Mutually beneficial cooperation has produced fruitful results, and the traditional friendship has taken root in the hearts of the people. China stands ready to work with Oman to steer the strategic partnership to a higher level," Xi said, according to Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning.

Haitham said China had become Oman’s largest trading partner, with direct investments by Chinese companies in partnership with the Oman Investment Authority exceeding 33 billion yuan ($4.6 billion) in recent years.

He expressed Oman’s willingness to conclude a preferential bilateral trade and investment agreement with China to further strengthen economic cooperation.

The sultan also called for expanded cooperation in renewable energy, artificial intelligence, digital technologies, space, defence industries, and logistics.

Oman is China's fifth-largest crude oil supplier and fourth-largest Arab trading partner, with bilateral trade volume reaching $36.73 billion in 2024.

The leaders agreed to expand cooperation in energy, investment, artificial intelligence, and technology, witnessing the signing of several agreements covering supply chains, green development, and digital finance.

The two sides signed at least 14 agreements, memoranda of understanding, and cooperation protocols, Oman News Agency reported.

Haitham highlighted the potential for cooperation between China’s Belt and Road Initiative and Oman Vision 2040, particularly in green hydrogen, advanced manufacturing, and digital infrastructure.

He reaffirmed Oman’s commitment to the one-China principle and expressed support for China’s territorial integrity and sovereignty.

headline: French school protests resume on smaller scale as students return from break
description: Police present, though not in full anti-riot gear as youth try to blockade high schools in Paris, Marseille, Rennes
author: Reuters
article_text:
French high school student protests resumed on Monday on a much smaller scale than in past weeks as pupils returned from a two-week break, with youngsters trying to blockade a few high schools in Paris, Marseille and Rennes, French media reported.

Hundreds of France's more than 3,000 high schools were blockaded in the weeks prior to the break. The protests, which began in the Paris suburbs in September, have spread across France and broadened beyond education to focus on the cost of living, drawing in trade unionists and activists and sometimes turning violent.

A wave of so-called "Gen Z" protests has swept across European countries including Germany, Italy, Belgium and Albania, driven by grievances including the cost of living, the poor state of schools and perceived corruption

Last month French protests degenerated into violent clashes with the police and outright riots in several cities, with shops looted, in a test for President Emmanuel Macron's minority government.

"In terms of blockades — or rather, attempted blockades — the phenomenon is very marginal. We're talking about just a handful of units, a few individual schools," Education Minister Edouard Geffray told radio station France Inter on Monday morning. He said protests are allowed but preventing access to schools is illegal.

Police officers were present, TV footage showed, though not in full anti-riot gear.

Students want the renovation of aging schools, more teachers, more university places and the end of a university admissions system they see as socially unfair.

Geffray offered last week to cap class sizes at 28, dedicate €4 billion ($4.47 billion) to renovating schools, create 15,000 new places for students in higher education and a new admission system by 2028. High school student representatives said the offers were not enough and they would keep protesting.

headline: Stylist Molly Dickson faces backlash as fans accuse her of giving Sadie Sink less effort compared to McKenna Grace
description: McKenna Grace’s recent red carpet appearances have fuelled comparisons with Sadie Sink’s understated looks
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Celebrity stylist Molly Dickson is facing criticism online after fans accused her of putting less effort into dressing Sadie Sink than her other high profile clients.

The debate gained traction after a viral post on X compared Sink’s recent red carpet appearances with glamorous looks worn by McKenna Grace, Sydney Sweeney and Bella Hadid. Some users argued that Sink’s outfits appeared less striking, while others questioned whether Dickson was making the most of the actress’s fashion moments.

Comparisons with Grace have attracted particular attention. During the promotional tour for The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping, Grace wore a romantic pink House of Gilles gown featuring floral details and a sheer corset. Sink, meanwhile, wore a Prada dress with platform sandals and a Fred Leighton diamond ring to the Spider-Man: Brand New Day premiere.

However, Sink’s relationship with Prada is an important part of the discussion. The actress was named an ambassador for the luxury fashion house in September and has worn its designs at several major events, including the 2025 Met Gala and the West End opening night of Romeo & Juliet.

View this post on Instagram

headline: Hudson Williams addresses whether he has romantic feelings for ‘Heated Rivalry’ co-star Connor Storrie
description: The 25-year-old actor addressed the question during his appearance on CBC’s ‘The Assembly‘
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Hudson Williams has spoken candidly about his close relationship with Heated Rivalry co-star Connor Storrie after being asked whether their friendship had ever developed into something romantic.

The 25-year-old actor addressed the question during his appearance on CBC’s The Assembly, which features celebrities and public figures answering questions from interviewers on the autism spectrum.

The episode premiered on Sunday, November 1, 2026.

During the interview, Williams was asked directly: “Did you ever feel something for Connor that was ‘more than friendship?’”

Responding thoughtfully, the actor explained that the pair had developed a particularly strong friendship rather than romantic feelings.

“No. Quickly, me and Connor realized we were, like, platonic soulmates, just completely in love with each other. I think that’s what made our friendship so stable and beautiful, is that we realized we could be completely ourselves, be completely guard down,” Hudson shared.

He continued by describing the affection and comfort they shared, adding: “So, I think the thing that made our relationship as rich as it was is, like, me and that man could cuddle for ten hours, and it just mean cuddling, just mean we just love each other dearly, but don’t wanna beep each other’s bop.”

“That’s not a saying,” he added, prompting laughter from the interviewers.

Williams and Storrie have previously discussed their close friendship during promotional interviews for the series.

The pair are currently filming the second season of Heated Rivalry, following the success of its debut season.

headline: Slavia face Arsenal as grim record looms
description: The Czech champions must overcome their European struggles to prevent an unwanted Champions League record
author: AFP
article_text:
Hosting Arsenal in the Champions League on Wednesday, Slavia Prague are facing the mammoth task of ending a drawn-out winless streak in the competition as an unwelcome record looms. The Czech champions have won a single game out of 23 in the Champions League -- on their debut in the competition against Steaua Bucharest in September 2007. They have since only managed eight draws and 14 losses over four Champions League campaigns including the current one. "Of course the longer it gets, the more unpleasant it is," said Jindrich Trpisovsky, the Slavia manager since 2017. "The streak is long and as we keep talking about it, I brood over it more than in the past," he added. Record holders AEK Athens failed to win 24 straight games from 1992-2006, while Steaua, now known as FCSB, recorded 23 winless games between 2006 and 2013. Slavia host Arsenal fresh off the back of their 1-0 victory over Liverpool at Anfield, which would daunt most teams, before Villarreal at home and Bayern Munich away in their next European games. "Of course we know how tough European games are and how hard you must work to win," said Trpisovsky. "In some games we were on the front foot and we got beaten. This is the beauty of football."

'Unlucky' Slavia have faced Arsenal three times in the Champions League, recording a draw and two losses including a humiliating 7-0 drubbing in London in 2007. "Slavia simply face the best teams whose quality is obvious," said Vladimir Smicer, a former Slavia striker who won the Champions League with Liverpool in 2005. "I think they were unlucky a few times," he told AFP. Slavia were close to breaking the hoodoo in this year's opener against Lens -- reduced to 10 men, they took a 2-1 lead in the 89th minute but squandered the chance and lost 3-2. "That's bad luck really. But the streak is unpleasant in any case," said Smicer, who played for Lens from 1996-1999. "And they are now facing teams like Arsenal and Bayern and these are games you don't expect Slavia to win." Smicer said Slavia should rather have beaten lower-ranked teams like Sabah to whom they lost 2-0 in Baku in October. "Slavia has a deep roster so the coach can adapt to the playing style of their opponents, but in the end it's all about quality," he added. "In Baku they simply underperformed, like in some other games, and that extended the winless streak. There have been games they should have won but unfortunately it didn't happen." Slavia will host Arsenal on November 4, exactly a year after losing 3-0 to the Gunners in the Champions League at home. Slavia defender David Zima hailed the competition as "a football university". "It's the top level and you can't stress out about having to win now. This is simply football and you can't always win. You just need a little luck." Trpisovsky said everything would have to click into place for Slavia to stand a chance against the giants. "Everything has to go our way and we need to give 100 percent and then we can succeed in any game."

Trpisovsky said everything would have to click into place for Slavia to stand a chance against the giants.

"Everything has to go our way and we need to give 100 percent and then we can succeed in any game."

headline: Arsenal ride out Liverpool storm to top Premier League
description: The Gunners strengthen their title defence with a hard-fought 1-0 victory over Liverpool
author: AFP
article_text:
Arsenal moved to the top of the Premier League with their first win away to Liverpool in 14 years as Kai Havertz's early strike secured a 1-0 victory for the Gunners. The defending champions were made to suffer after the German's 16th-minute opener but held out for what could be a telling win in their quest to retain the title. Arsenal climbed three points clear of Manchester City at the top of the table. But with City expected to be hit with a severe points penalty, unless they can overturn a guilty verdict on over 100 charges of breaking Premier League rules, Arsenal dealt a huge blow to their most likely rivals for the title. "It's been such a long time without this feeling here, that we really needed it," said Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta. "We are extremely proud of what the team, the players, everybody has done." Liverpool produced arguably their best spell of Andoni Iraola's early months in charge with a blistering 30 minutes after conceding, but failed to take their chances as the Spaniard suffered just his second defeat in 14 games since arriving from Bournemouth. Arteta was stinging in his criticism of the Arsenal side that crashed out to fourth-tier Fleetwood on Tuesday in one of the biggest ever League Cup shocks. The Arsenal boss got the response he desired in a strong start from the champions. Havertz was one of the biggest culprits for wasting chances in midweek but made amends with a simple finish from Declan Rice's precise low cross. The early goal lit the touchpaper for a pulsating first 45 minutes as Liverpool roared back.

Isak honesty saves Arsenal

Iraola and Arteta played together as boys for Basque side Antiguoko Kirol Elkartea. Arteta's old friend gave his side one of the most uncomfortable afternoons they have experienced in recent seasons as Arsenal's rock-solid defence was left clinging on for half-time. "I loved the reaction from my players after going 1-0 down," said Iraola. "I loved a lot of moments of the game. "We have to keep going. It is very early in the season. Arsenal are in the best of the situations but it is just the start of November today." All of Liverpool's three £100 million-plus ($134 million) forwards started together and there are signs the relationship between Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola is beginning to flourish. Isak did Arsenal a favour by not going down as he was pulled back by Jurrien Timber when just failing to connect with a wicked delivery from Barcola. "The Alex one is a clear penalty," added Iraola. "We can all see that he holds the shirt (but) because he doesn't go to the floor, you are not going to call the penalty? I don't understand it." Wirtz curled a free-kick onto the bar from a narrow angle and Alexis Mac Allister should have buried a header into the goal rather than finding the stand behind David Raya's goal. Half-time allowed Arsenal the chance to reset and take the wind out of Liverpool's sails as Iraola's men tired in the second period. Alisson Becker produced a stunning save to turn behind Christos Tzolis's shot that was arrowing into the bottom corner to keep Liverpool in the game. That intervention counted for little as Arsenal rode out the closing stages to register another clean sheet and an eighth win in nine league games. Defeat leaves fifth-placed Liverpool nine points adrift of the leaders and already facing a mountain to climb to get back in the title race.

headline: Lahore's AQI soars to 535 early morning as air pollution reaches hazardous levels
description: Gujranwala records AQI of 606 in the morning, Faisalabad, Multan records 310 each, Sialkot records 260
author: ADNAN LODHI
article_text:
Air pollution in Lahore intensified on Monday, with the provincial capital recording an Air Quality Index (AQI) of 535 and fine particulate matter (PM2.5) reaching 343 micrograms per cubic metre at 8am, exposing millions of residents to dangerously polluted air.

The reading, reported by IQAir and confirmed by the Punjab Environmental Protection Department (EPD), was among the most alarming pollution spikes recorded during the 2026 smog season. Smog and air pollution also covered several parts of the city and its surrounding areas.

The regional situation was equally concerning. Gujranwala recorded an AQI of 606 in the morning, while Faisalabad and Multan registered readings of 310 each and Sialkot recorded 260. Lahore also topped IQAir's ranking of pollution levels in major cities in an early morning snapshot, although international rankings fluctuated throughout the day.

The deterioration raised fresh questions about the effectiveness of the government's anti-smog operations, particularly as agricultural burning, industrial emissions, vehicular pollution and construction dust continued to contribute to the pollution burden across Lahore and neighbouring districts.

The crisis extended beyond the provincial capital, with Sheikhupura, Kasur, Gujranwala, Nankana Sahib and other agricultural and industrial districts forming part of the wider pollution belt surrounding Lahore. Industrial fuel consumption, brick kilns, agricultural residue burning, waste disposal practices and transport emissions collectively added to the regional pollution burden.

A particularly concerning development emerged from satellite observations of agricultural fires across Punjab. According to an analysis of data from the environmental monitoring website, NASA satellites detected 13,241 fire spots in Pakistani Punjab between October 1 and 29, compared with 3,158 in Indian Punjab.

Around 92 per cent of the detected fires in Pakistani Punjab were located on farmland and were considered likely to be associated with crop residue burning. Okara recorded the highest number of fire spots at 2,144, followed by Gujranwala with 1,011 and Nankana Sahib with 1,003.

The findings were significant for Lahore because the affected agricultural districts fell within the wider regional airshed. However, satellite fire detections alone could not establish how much smoke from individual fires contributed to the city's measured AQI.

The figures raised questions about the geographical limitations of Punjab's anti-smog strategy and whether Lahore could achieve cleaner air while pollution-producing activities continued across surrounding agricultural and industrial districts.

Another concern was the gap between reported improvements in air quality and actual reductions in pollution emissions.

A recent assessment by the Pakistan Air Quality Initiative (PAQI) found that average PM2.5 concentrations across 26 monitoring sites in Lahore had declined by 27 per cent in October compared with the same month last year. However, its weather-adjusted analysis estimated that improvements attributable to factors other than weather amounted to only around four per cent.

The assessment also found that PM2.5 concentrations had remained above Pakistan's prescribed daily limit on every day of October. The findings suggested that favourable atmospheric conditions had contributed substantially to the comparatively better air quality, rather than indicating a decisive structural reduction in pollution sources.

The renewed deterioration in November therefore raised questions about whether the Punjab government's enforcement measures were delivering sustainable results or whether temporary weather conditions had provided much of the relief.

The health implications were particularly serious. PM2.5 particles are small enough to penetrate deep into the lungs and enter the bloodstream, increasing the risk of respiratory and cardiovascular complications. Children, older people, outdoor workers and individuals with existing respiratory conditions remained particularly vulnerable.

The pollution also affected everyday economic and social activities, including outdoor employment, school attendance, public transport and commercial operations. Residents who spent long hours commuting on motorcycles or working on roads faced prolonged exposure to polluted air.

Environmental experts have repeatedly emphasised that controlling smog requires more than temporary restrictions and emergency operations. Industrial emission monitoring, cleaner transport, effective construction dust management, restrictions on open waste burning, modernised brick kilns and alternatives to agricultural residue burning need to form part of a sustained strategy.

For Lahore, this would require extending anti-smog enforcement beyond municipal boundaries through coordinated action involving the Punjab Environmental Protection and Climate Change Department, district administrations, agriculture authorities, industrial regulators and local governments.

The provincial government also needed to introduce transparent, district-wise pollution monitoring, publish inspection and enforcement records, strengthen industrial emissions testing and ensure that repeat environmental violators faced meaningful penalties.

A regional airshed management mechanism could help identify major pollution sources, assess their contributions and coordinate preventive measures across districts, rather than treating each city as an isolated environmental unit.

Responding to the situation, EPD official spokesperson Sajid Bashir said the department's efforts had helped improve air quality compared with October last year, although the authorities were still working to tackle pollution.

"Due to the efforts of the Punjab government and the Environment Department, smog and pollution levels were better this October than last year. We are still working hard to tackle the pollution situation," he said.

With Lahore recording an AQI above 530 and neighbouring cities also experiencing hazardous pollution, the latest episode exposed a fundamental weakness in the province's approach.

The challenge was no longer simply how to clear the smog over Lahore, but how to control pollution generated across the wider region. Without measurable reductions in emissions and coordinated enforcement across Punjab, emergency anti-smog operations risked providing only temporary relief while the underlying environmental crisis continued.

article_html:
LAHORE:

Air pollution in Lahore intensified on Monday, with the provincial capital recording an Air Quality Index (AQI) of 535 and fine particulate matter (PM2.5) reaching 343 micrograms per cubic metre at 8am, exposing millions of residents to dangerously polluted air.

The reading, reported by IQAir and confirmed by the Punjab Environmental Protection Department (EPD), was among the most alarming pollution spikes recorded during the 2026 smog season. Smog and air pollution also covered several parts of the city and its surrounding areas.

The regional situation was equally concerning. Gujranwala recorded an AQI of 606 in the morning, while Faisalabad and Multan registered readings of 310 each and Sialkot recorded 260. Lahore also topped IQAir's ranking of pollution levels in major cities in an early morning snapshot, although international rankings fluctuated throughout the day.

The deterioration raised fresh questions about the effectiveness of the government's anti-smog operations, particularly as agricultural burning, industrial emissions, vehicular pollution and construction dust continued to contribute to the pollution burden across Lahore and neighbouring districts.

Get hourly AQI updates, area-wise rankings, and health advisories from Punjab EPA's official website.https://t.co/2wAZKiJMXP#epapunjab #publicawareness #cleanair #aqi #aqilahore pic.twitter.com/VPGMIYZKni

— @EPCCDPUNJAB (@EPCCDpunjab) November 2, 2026

The crisis extended beyond the provincial capital, with Sheikhupura, Kasur, Gujranwala, Nankana Sahib and other agricultural and industrial districts forming part of the wider pollution belt surrounding Lahore. Industrial fuel consumption, brick kilns, agricultural residue burning, waste disposal practices and transport emissions collectively added to the regional pollution burden.

A particularly concerning development emerged from satellite observations of agricultural fires across Punjab. According to an analysis of data from the environmental monitoring website, NASA satellites detected 13,241 fire spots in Pakistani Punjab between October 1 and 29, compared with 3,158 in Indian Punjab.

Around 92 per cent of the detected fires in Pakistani Punjab were located on farmland and were considered likely to be associated with crop residue burning. Okara recorded the highest number of fire spots at 2,144, followed by Gujranwala with 1,011 and Nankana Sahib with 1,003.

The findings were significant for Lahore because the affected agricultural districts fell within the wider regional airshed. However, satellite fire detections alone could not establish how much smoke from individual fires contributed to the city's measured AQI.

The figures raised questions about the geographical limitations of Punjab's anti-smog strategy and whether Lahore could achieve cleaner air while pollution-producing activities continued across surrounding agricultural and industrial districts.

Read: October pollution less than last year

Another concern was the gap between reported improvements in air quality and actual reductions in pollution emissions.

A recent assessment by the Pakistan Air Quality Initiative (PAQI) found that average PM2.5 concentrations across 26 monitoring sites in Lahore had declined by 27 per cent in October compared with the same month last year. However, its weather-adjusted analysis estimated that improvements attributable to factors other than weather amounted to only around four per cent.

The assessment also found that PM2.5 concentrations had remained above Pakistan's prescribed daily limit on every day of October. The findings suggested that favourable atmospheric conditions had contributed substantially to the comparatively better air quality, rather than indicating a decisive structural reduction in pollution sources.

The renewed deterioration in November therefore raised questions about whether the Punjab government's enforcement measures were delivering sustainable results or whether temporary weather conditions had provided much of the relief.

The health implications were particularly serious. PM2.5 particles are small enough to penetrate deep into the lungs and enter the bloodstream, increasing the risk of respiratory and cardiovascular complications. Children, older people, outdoor workers and individuals with existing respiratory conditions remained particularly vulnerable.

The pollution also affected everyday economic and social activities, including outdoor employment, school attendance, public transport and commercial operations. Residents who spent long hours commuting on motorcycles or working on roads faced prolonged exposure to polluted air.

Environmental experts have repeatedly emphasised that controlling smog requires more than temporary restrictions and emergency operations. Industrial emission monitoring, cleaner transport, effective construction dust management, restrictions on open waste burning, modernised brick kilns and alternatives to agricultural residue burning need to form part of a sustained strategy.

Read more: Drone-based smoke monitoring fails

For Lahore, this would require extending anti-smog enforcement beyond municipal boundaries through coordinated action involving the Punjab Environmental Protection and Climate Change Department, district administrations, agriculture authorities, industrial regulators and local governments.

The provincial government also needed to introduce transparent, district-wise pollution monitoring, publish inspection and enforcement records, strengthen industrial emissions testing and ensure that repeat environmental violators faced meaningful penalties.

A regional airshed management mechanism could help identify major pollution sources, assess their contributions and coordinate preventive measures across districts, rather than treating each city as an isolated environmental unit.

Responding to the situation, EPD official spokesperson Sajid Bashir said the department's efforts had helped improve air quality compared with October last year, although the authorities were still working to tackle pollution.

"Due to the efforts of the Punjab government and the Environment Department, smog and pollution levels were better this October than last year. We are still working hard to tackle the pollution situation," he said.

With Lahore recording an AQI above 530 and neighbouring cities also experiencing hazardous pollution, the latest episode exposed a fundamental weakness in the province's approach.

The challenge was no longer simply how to clear the smog over Lahore, but how to control pollution generated across the wider region. Without measurable reductions in emissions and coordinated enforcement across Punjab, emergency anti-smog operations risked providing only temporary relief while the underlying environmental crisis continued.

The figures raised questions about the geographical limitations of Punjab's anti-smog strategy and whether Lahore could achieve cleaner air while pollution-producing activities continued across surrounding agricultural and industrial districts.

Another concern was the gap between reported improvements in air quality and actual reductions in pollution emissions.

A recent assessment by the Pakistan Air Quality Initiative (PAQI) found that average PM2.5 concentrations across 26 monitoring sites in Lahore had declined by 27 per cent in October compared with the same month last year. However, its weather-adjusted analysis estimated that improvements attributable to factors other than weather amounted to only around four per cent.

The assessment also found that PM2.5 concentrations had remained above Pakistan's prescribed daily limit on every day of October. The findings suggested that favourable atmospheric conditions had contributed substantially to the comparatively better air quality, rather than indicating a decisive structural reduction in pollution sources.

The renewed deterioration in November therefore raised questions about whether the Punjab government's enforcement measures were delivering sustainable results or whether temporary weather conditions had provided much of the relief.

The health implications were particularly serious. PM2.5 particles are small enough to penetrate deep into the lungs and enter the bloodstream, increasing the risk of respiratory and cardiovascular complications. Children, older people, outdoor workers and individuals with existing respiratory conditions remained particularly vulnerable.

The pollution also affected everyday economic and social activities, including outdoor employment, school attendance, public transport and commercial operations. Residents who spent long hours commuting on motorcycles or working on roads faced prolonged exposure to polluted air.

Environmental experts have repeatedly emphasised that controlling smog requires more than temporary restrictions and emergency operations. Industrial emission monitoring, cleaner transport, effective construction dust management, restrictions on open waste burning, modernised brick kilns and alternatives to agricultural residue burning need to form part of a sustained strategy.

For Lahore, this would require extending anti-smog enforcement beyond municipal boundaries through coordinated action involving the Punjab Environmental Protection and Climate Change Department, district administrations, agriculture authorities, industrial regulators and local governments.

The provincial government also needed to introduce transparent, district-wise pollution monitoring, publish inspection and enforcement records, strengthen industrial emissions testing and ensure that repeat environmental violators faced meaningful penalties.

A regional airshed management mechanism could help identify major pollution sources, assess their contributions and coordinate preventive measures across districts, rather than treating each city as an isolated environmental unit.

Responding to the situation, EPD official spokesperson Sajid Bashir said the department's efforts had helped improve air quality compared with October last year, although the authorities were still working to tackle pollution.

"Due to the efforts of the Punjab government and the Environment Department, smog and pollution levels were better this October than last year. We are still working hard to tackle the pollution situation," he said.

With Lahore recording an AQI above 530 and neighbouring cities also experiencing hazardous pollution, the latest episode exposed a fundamental weakness in the province's approach.

The challenge was no longer simply how to clear the smog over Lahore, but how to control pollution generated across the wider region. Without measurable reductions in emissions and coordinated enforcement across Punjab, emergency anti-smog operations risked providing only temporary relief while the underlying environmental crisis continued.

headline: Messi inspires Miami comeback against New England
description: The Argentine superstar inspires a comeback with a goal and an assist in 2-1 victory
author: AFP
article_text: Lionel Messi's late strike catapulted Inter Miami above New England and into second place with a tense 2-1 comeback victory over their MLS Eastern Conference rivals Sunday. Messi's typically crafty effort after scurrying through three defenders in the 83rd minute was enough to secure three points, with an own goal by his teammate Ian Fray four minutes later ruled out for a marginal offside. The 39-year-old Argentine superstar also provided an improvised assist off the back of his head for German Berterame, after Daniel Gazdag had put New England in front early in the second half. Victory sent Miami a point clear of the New England Revolution with one game left, meaning a win against Charlotte on Saturday will guarantee home advantage until the Conference Finals. It also secured Miami's spot in next year's CONCACAF Champions Cup. "It was such an important occasion...they're a very tough team -- really difficult -- so I think it was a tremendous effort," said Berterame. After a goalless first half, New England's Peyton Miller slipped down the right flank to the byline in the 53rd minute. His cut-back pass was backheeled by Ilay Feingold to Gazdag, who smashed the ball home. Miami came close to equalizing soon after the hour, as Berterame followed up on a Messi effort saved by Matt Turner, only to have his shot cleared off the line by Brooklyn Raines. In the 69th minute, Telasco Segovia flicked a ball high into the box toward Messi, who was racing forward between two defenders but somehow headed it blindly off the back of his head to Berterame, who scored. Messi got on the scoresheet himself in the 83rd minute, collecting the ball just outside the D, spinning and skipping past three tackles before wrapping his left foot around the ball and sending it low into the far corner past US national team goalkeeper Turner. New England thought they had been gifted an equalizer with three minutes remaining. Fray inexplicably headed a hopeful Luca Langoni cross into his own net despite no pressure, but the New England substitute was ruled offside on video review. The Eastern Conference's final playoff berths were also determined Sunday. Columbus Crew and Orlando City both qualified after 10th-placed New York Red Bulls lost 3-2 to runaway leaders Nashville. Sam Sturridge's stoppage-time strike sealed a comeback victory from 2-0 down for Nashville, who have tied the record for the most points in MLS history, on 74, with a game still to play. Nashville lifted the Supporters' Shield trophy on Sunday at their Geodis Park stadium, where they have not lost all year, becoming the first team in MLS history with 15 home wins. Higher seeds retain home advantage through the post-season until the MLS Cup, which will take place on December 18.

headline: LHC recognises daily-wage employees as permanent workers in Punjab health authorities
description: Court rules workers acquire permanent status after 9 months, regardless of formal notifications by health authorities
author: Web Desk
article_text:
The Lahore High Court (LHC) has ruled that daily-wage and work-charged employees serving against posts of a permanent nature in Punjab's District Health Authorities (DHAs) acquire the status of permanent workmen after completing the prescribed period of nine months, regardless of whether the authorities issue formal notifications recognising their status.

Allowing a batch of constitutional petitions, Justice Khalid Ishaq held that the Punjab government's 2021 policy governing daily-wage, work-charged and contingent-paid employees was applicable to DHAs and could not be avoided on the grounds that the authorities were autonomous bodies.

In a detailed judgment in Muhammad Bilal Raza and others vs Government of Punjab and others (2026 LHC 8384), the court declared the government's refusal to grant eligible employees permanent status unlawful and set aside the orders through which the authorities had rejected their requests.

The petitioners, including data entry operators, sanitary workers and a laboratory assistant, were employed at various public health facilities across Punjab. Most had initially been appointed for 89 days, with their contracts repeatedly extended over several years despite the continuing nature of their work.

The judgment noted that some employees had been working since 2016 and 2017, while others had served for shorter periods. Several approached the High Court after their requests for recognition as permanent employees were rejected.

Some also complained that their services had been discontinued through verbal orders, while similarly placed employees in other districts had already been granted permanent-workman status.

The government departments and DHAs opposed the petitions, arguing that the authorities were autonomous bodies and therefore not covered by the 2021 policy issued by the Services and General Administration Department (S&GAD). Some also maintained that the petitioners did not qualify as skilled workers and cited financial constraints.

Rejecting the autonomy argument, the court referred to Rule 10(c) of the Punjab District Health Authorities (Conduct of Business) Rules, 2016, which requires a DHA's chief executive officer to implement standards and policies prescribed by the government.

The judge held that there was no plausible justification for the DHAs to refuse to implement the 2021 policy, adding that its provisions applied to their daily-wage and contingent-paid employees. The judgment also distinguished between regularisation as a civil servant and recognition as a permanent workman under labour laws.

Referring to the Industrial and Commercial Employment (Standing Orders) Ordinance, 1968, the court noted that a permanent workman was defined as an employee, skilled or unskilled, engaged in work of a permanent nature likely to last more than nine months, who had satisfactorily completed a three-month probationary period.

The court relied on the Supreme Court's ruling in Province of Punjab vs Ahmad Hussain (2013 SCMR 1547), which recognised that daily-wage and work-charged employees continuously performing work of a permanent nature beyond nine months could acquire the status of permanent workmen.

It observed that the nature of the work, rather than the employee's designation or temporary mode of appointment, was decisive in determining their legal status.

The judge further held that the provisions of the 2021 policy were "self-executory", meaning eligible employees acquired permanent-workman status by operation of law without requiring a separate notification from the authorities.

The court also rejected the argument that employees who had been laid off or whose short-term appointments had not been extended could no longer claim protection under the policy.

Citing the Supreme Court's judgment in Town Administration and another vs Mohammad Khalid and others (2024 SCMR 1852), the High Court observed that repeatedly engaging employees through short-term or daily-wage arrangements could not be used as a device to circumvent protections available under labour laws.

The court further noted that the Standing Orders required employers to provide employment conditions in writing and communicate termination, removal, retrenchment, discharge or dismissal through a written order explicitly stating the reasons.

Citing a Supreme Court verdict on workers' rights, the judgment stated, "Verbal termination of service is alien to labour and service laws and is also contrary to the principles of natural justice, good governance, fairness and transparency."

It also addressed the petitioners' allegations of discriminatory treatment.

The employees had produced departmental orders showing that similarly placed daily-wage workers had already been granted permanent-workman status in various districts. Invoking Article 25 of the Constitution, which guarantees equality before the law, the court observed that the authorities had failed to establish any reasonable distinction between those employees and the petitioners.

It held that granting benefits to some employees while denying them to others in similar circumstances was not legally sustainable.

On outstanding salaries, however, the court did not directly order the payment of all dues claimed by the petitioners.

"The question of disbursement of outstanding remuneration/salaries of the Petitioner(s) shall be decided through separate order(s) by the Respondents/Authorities after affording a meaningful opportunity of hearing to the Petitioner(s) on the basis of the available record," the judgment stated.

It directed that where it was established that an employee had continued performing duties during the disputed period, the outstanding remuneration would have to be paid. However, in cases where no services had been rendered, the authorities could apply the principle of "no work, no pay".

The ruling reinforces the legal protections available to long-serving daily-wage and work-charged employees in Punjab's public health system, requiring the concerned authorities to implement the government's policy in accordance with labour laws.

The judgment noted that some employees had been working since 2016 and 2017, while others had served for shorter periods. Several approached the High Court after their requests for recognition as permanent employees were rejected.
Some also complained that their services had been discontinued through verbal orders, while similarly placed employees in other districts had already been granted permanent-workman status.

The government departments and DHAs opposed the petitions, arguing that the authorities were autonomous bodies and therefore not covered by the 2021 policy issued by the Services and General Administration Department (S&GAD). Some also maintained that the petitioners did not qualify as skilled workers and cited financial constraints.

Rejecting the autonomy argument, the court referred to Rule 10(c) of the Punjab District Health Authorities (Conduct of Business) Rules, 2016, which requires a DHA's chief executive officer to implement standards and policies prescribed by the government.

The judge held that there was no plausible justification for the DHAs to refuse to implement the 2021 policy, adding that its provisions applied to their daily-wage and contingent-paid employees. The judgment also distinguished between regularisation as a civil servant and recognition as a permanent workman under labour laws.

Referring to the Industrial and Commercial Employment (Standing Orders) Ordinance, 1968, the court noted that a permanent workman was defined as an employee, skilled or unskilled, engaged in work of a permanent nature likely to last more than nine months, who had satisfactorily completed a three-month probationary period.

The court relied on the Supreme Court's ruling in Province of Punjab vs Ahmad Hussain (2013 SCMR 1547), which recognised that daily-wage and work-charged employees continuously performing work of a permanent nature beyond nine months could acquire the status of permanent workmen.
It observed that the nature of the work, rather than the employee's designation or temporary mode of appointment, was decisive in determining their legal status.

The judge further held that the provisions of the 2021 policy were "self-executory", meaning eligible employees acquired permanent-workman status by operation of law without requiring a separate notification from the authorities.
The court also rejected the argument that employees who had been laid off or whose short-term appointments had not been extended could no longer claim protection under the policy.

Citing the Supreme Court's judgment in Town Administration and another vs Mohammad Khalid and others (2024 SCMR 1852), the High Court observed that repeatedly engaging employees through short-term or daily-wage arrangements could not be used as a device to circumvent protections available under labour laws.

The court further noted that the Standing Orders required employers to provide employment conditions in writing and communicate termination, removal, retrenchment, discharge or dismissal through a written order explicitly stating the reasons.

Citing a Supreme Court verdict on workers' rights, the judgment stated, "Verbal termination of service is alien to labour and service laws and is also contrary to the principles of natural justice, good governance, fairness and transparency."
It also addressed the petitioners' allegations of discriminatory treatment.

The employees had produced departmental orders showing that similarly placed daily-wage workers had already been granted permanent-workman status in various districts. Invoking Article 25 of the Constitution, which guarantees equality before the law, the court observed that the authorities had failed to establish any reasonable distinction between those employees and the petitioners.
It held that granting benefits to some employees while denying them to others in similar circumstances was not legally sustainable.
On outstanding salaries, however, the court did not directly order the payment of all dues claimed by the petitioners.

"The question of disbursement of outstanding remuneration/salaries of the Petitioner(s) shall be decided through separate order(s) by the Respondents/Authorities after affording a meaningful opportunity of hearing to the Petitioner(s) on the basis of the available record," the judgment stated.

It directed that where it was established that an employee had continued performing duties during the disputed period, the outstanding remuneration would have to be paid. However, in cases where no services had been rendered, the authorities could apply the principle of "no work, no pay".

The ruling reinforces the legal protections available to long-serving daily-wage and work-charged employees in Punjab's public health system, requiring the concerned authorities to implement the government's policy in accordance with labour laws.

headline: Mara Wilson and Danny DeVito reunite with ‘Matilda’ cast for film’s 30th anniversary
description: Wilson thanked her former co-stars, recalling the lifelong friendships formed during filming
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Mara Wilson and Danny DeVito reunited with their Matilda co-stars in London to mark the beloved film’s 30th anniversary, surprising audiences at a special screening of the 1996 classic.

The celebration took place on October 30 at the Royal Albert Hall, where DeVito hosted a live-narrated screening accompanied by the Royal Philharmonic Concert Orchestra. The orchestra performed composer David Newman’s score as the film played for the audience.

View this post on Instagram

DeVito, who directed the adaptation and portrayed Matilda’s father, Harry Wormwood, announced that several former cast members had joined him for the occasion. Wilson, who played the title character, appeared alongside Pam Ferris, Kiami Davael, Jacqueline Steiger and Kira Spencer Hesser.

Ferris portrayed the formidable Miss Trunchbull, while Davael played Lavender, Steiger appeared as Amanda Thripp and Spencer Hesser portrayed Hortensia. Their surprise appearance prompted an enthusiastic response from the audience.

Wilson later shared photographs from the reunion on Instagram, expressing her happiness at celebrating with people who had remained important to her over the years.

View this post on Instagram

The actress also revealed that approximately 5,000 fans attended the anniversary event. She thanked her former co-stars, Newman and DeVito, whom she affectionately called Uncle Danny, while reflecting on the memories they shared during production.

Released in July 1996, Matilda was adapted from Roald Dahl’s children’s novel. The story follows a gifted young girl who discovers her abilities while dealing with an unkind family and an intimidating school headmistress.

The reunion also recalled the close bond Wilson developed with DeVito and his wife, Rhea Perlman, during filming. Wilson has previously spoken about how the couple supported her and her family while her mother was receiving treatment for breast cancer.

Three decades after its release, Matilda continues to hold a special place for its cast and audiences, with the London gathering bringing several of its familiar faces together again.

headline: US midterms: Polls show Democrats ahead in battle for Congress
description: National surveys give Democrats advantage in House races while latest state polls show gains in Senate battlegrounds
author: Anadolu Agency
article_text:
Democrats lead Republicans in national polling ahead of Tuesday's United States midterm elections, with new surveys showing the party gaining ground in several closely contested Senate races as voters express dissatisfaction with President Donald Trump's handling of the economy.

With all 435 House of Representatives seats and 35 Senate seats on the ballot, the elections will determine whether Republicans retain control of Congress for the remaining two years of Trump's second term.

A RealClearPolling average of surveys conducted through October 30 shows Democrats leading Republicans 52% to 43.1% on the generic congressional ballot, an 8.9-percentage-point advantage. An NBC News survey conducted October 28-30 found Democrats ahead 52% to 45%, while an Emerson College poll conducted October 24-26 put the gap at 10 points.

The generic ballot measures nationwide preferences for congressional candidates rather than support in individual districts, meaning a national lead does not necessarily translate into a corresponding number of House seats.

House: Democrats lead nationally

Republicans currently control the House, where 218 seats are needed for a majority.

The nonpartisan Cook Political Report's latest ratings, updated Friday, place 222 districts in categories favoring Democrats and 195 favouring Republicans, with another 18 classified as toss-ups. Of the 18 toss-up districts, 14 are currently held by Republicans and four by Democrats.

Cook shifted another 12 House races toward Democrats on October 30, including Republican-held districts in Colorado and Pennsylvania, reflecting changes in its assessment of the electoral landscape.

Among the closely watched contests are California's 22nd District, where Republican Representative David Valadao faces Democrat Randy Villegas; New York's 17th, where Republican Representative Mike Lawler faces Democrat Cait Conley; and Texas' 15th, where Republican Representative Monica De La Cruz faces Democrat Bobby Pulido.

Republicans are also contesting Democratic-held seats in Florida, North Carolina and Texas, where redistricting has altered the electoral landscape. However, district-level polling remains uneven, and the national figures offer only a broad indication of the environment in which individual races are being fought.

Senate: Democrats gain ground in battlegrounds

The battle for the Senate is more complicated. Republicans hold 53 seats, compared with 47 held by Democrats and two independents who caucus with them.

Democrats need a net gain of four seats to secure a majority. A 50-50 split would leave Republicans in control because Vice President JD Vance can cast tie-breaking votes.

The latest New York Times/Siena University polls, conducted from October 23-November 1, show Democratic candidates ahead in six of seven key Senate battlegrounds and effectively tied with Republicans in the seventh. Five of those Democratic leads are in Republican-held states, including Texas and Kansas, which have not elected Democratic senators since 1988 and 1932, respectively.

In Michigan, the only Democratic-held seat among the seven surveyed, Abdul El-Sayed leads Republican Mike Rogers 53% to 42%, an 11-point advantage.

In Texas, Democrat James Talarico leads Republican Ken Paxton 50% to 43%, while in Maine, Democratic challenger Troy Jackson has 51% support against Republican Senator Susan Collins' 45%.

Former Democratic Senator Sherrod Brown leads Republican Senator Jon Husted 49% to 44% in Ohio, while Democrat Adam Hamilton leads Republican incumbent Roger Marshall by the same margin in Kansas.

The contests are tighter in Alaska and Iowa. In Alaska, Democrat Mary Peltola leads Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan 48% to 46%, while Iowa Democrat Josh Turek is effectively tied with Republican Ashley Hinson, 48% to 47%.

The surveys show Democrats improving their position since September in six of the seven states.

Maine shifted from a three-point Republican lead in September to a six-point Democratic advantage, while Michigan's Democratic lead widened from five to 11 points. Kansas moved from a tie to a five-point Democratic lead, while Alaska was the only state where Democrats lost ground, with their advantage narrowing from seven points to approximately one point.

The surveys did not include North Carolina, another Republican-held seat where recent polling has consistently shown Democrat Roy Cooper leading Republican Michael Whatley.

The latest findings are not uniform across pollsters, and several battleground contests remain close in broader polling averages.

Trump's approval and voter priorities

The New York Times/Siena surveys found that just 38% of likely voters across the seven battleground states approved of Trump's job performance. Democratic candidates also led among independent voters in every state surveyed, while respondents expressed greater trust in Democrats on the cost of living, foreign wars and protecting the interests of ordinary people.

Across the seven states, Democratic candidates held a nine-point advantage over Republicans on handling the cost of living.

The findings are consistent with broader national dissatisfaction. An Associated Press-NORC survey conducted on October 8-12 found that 36% of voters approved of Trump's job performance, while 64% disapproved.

The economy and cost of living emerged as the leading election concerns, cited as important voting issues by 85% and 84% of respondents, respectively. Health care followed at 69%, while 64% identified the war with Iran as an important issue.

The survey also found that 47% of voters wanted Democrats to control the House, compared with 38% who preferred Republicans. For the Senate, the figures were 46% and 38%, respectively.

What the polls cannot predict

Despite Democrats' polling advantage, uncertainties surrounding turnout and survey accuracy could affect the results.

The New York Times/Siena polls, which surveyed between 610 and 1,215 likely voters in each state, had margins of sampling error ranging from 3.3 to 4.8 percentage points. They also found that voters who made their decisions during the preceding month favoured Republicans by nine points, indicating that late shifts in support could matter.

Polling errors can arise from inaccurate turnout assumptions, difficulties reaching certain demographic groups and systematic biases shared by multiple surveys.

The surveys also found that Democrats' support among some key demographic groups had strengthened since September, although polling has historically struggled to accurately measure white working-class voters.

With several Senate contests separated by only a few percentage points, small differences between polling estimates and actual voting patterns could change the balance of power in Congress.

article_html:
Democrats lead Republicans in national polling ahead of Tuesday's United States midterm elections, with new surveys showing the party gaining ground in several closely contested Senate races as voters express dissatisfaction with President Donald Trump's handling of the economy.

With all 435 House of Representatives seats and 35 Senate seats on the ballot, the elections will determine whether Republicans retain control of Congress for the remaining two years of Trump's second term.

A RealClearPolling average of surveys conducted through October 30 shows Democrats leading Republicans 52% to 43.1% on the generic congressional ballot, an 8.9-percentage-point advantage. An NBC News survey conducted October 28-30 found Democrats ahead 52% to 45%, while an Emerson College poll conducted October 24-26 put the gap at 10 points.

The generic ballot measures nationwide preferences for congressional candidates rather than support in individual districts, meaning a national lead does not necessarily translate into a corresponding number of House seats.

House: Democrats lead nationally

Republicans currently control the House, where 218 seats are needed for a majority.

The nonpartisan Cook Political Report's latest ratings, updated Friday, place 222 districts in categories favoring Democrats and 195 favouring Republicans, with another 18 classified as toss-ups. Of the 18 toss-up districts, 14 are currently held by Republicans and four by Democrats.

Cook shifted another 12 House races toward Democrats on October 30, including Republican-held districts in Colorado and Pennsylvania, reflecting changes in its assessment of the electoral landscape.

Read: Michigan Senate race a test of attacks on Muslim candidate, progressive agenda

Among the closely watched contests are California's 22nd District, where Republican Representative David Valadao faces Democrat Randy Villegas; New York's 17th, where Republican Representative Mike Lawler faces Democrat Cait Conley; and Texas' 15th, where Republican Representative Monica De La Cruz faces Democrat Bobby Pulido.

Republicans are also contesting Democratic-held seats in Florida, North Carolina and Texas, where redistricting has altered the electoral landscape. However, district-level polling remains uneven, and the national figures offer only a broad indication of the environment in which individual races are being fought.

Senate: Democrats gain ground in battlegrounds

The battle for the Senate is more complicated. Republicans hold 53 seats, compared with 47 held by Democrats and two independents who caucus with them.

Democrats need a net gain of four seats to secure a majority. A 50-50 split would leave Republicans in control because Vice President JD Vance can cast tie-breaking votes.

The latest New York Times/Siena University polls, conducted from October 23-November 1, show Democratic candidates ahead in six of seven key Senate battlegrounds and effectively tied with Republicans in the seventh. Five of those Democratic leads are in Republican-held states, including Texas and Kansas, which have not elected Democratic senators since 1988 and 1932, respectively.

In Michigan, the only Democratic-held seat among the seven surveyed, Abdul El-Sayed leads Republican Mike Rogers 53% to 42%, an 11-point advantage.

In Texas, Democrat James Talarico leads Republican Ken Paxton 50% to 43%, while in Maine, Democratic challenger Troy Jackson has 51% support against Republican Senator Susan Collins' 45%.

Former Democratic Senator Sherrod Brown leads Republican Senator Jon Husted 49% to 44% in Ohio, while Democrat Adam Hamilton leads Republican incumbent Roger Marshall by the same margin in Kansas.

The contests are tighter in Alaska and Iowa. In Alaska, Democrat Mary Peltola leads Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan 48% to 46%, while Iowa Democrat Josh Turek is effectively tied with Republican Ashley Hinson, 48% to 47%.

The surveys show Democrats improving their position since September in six of the seven states.

Read More: Trump rallies Republicans for midterms

Maine shifted from a three-point Republican lead in September to a six-point Democratic advantage, while Michigan's Democratic lead widened from five to 11 points. Kansas moved from a tie to a five-point Democratic lead, while Alaska was the only state where Democrats lost ground, with their advantage narrowing from seven points to approximately one point.

The surveys did not include North Carolina, another Republican-held seat where recent polling has consistently shown Democrat Roy Cooper leading Republican Michael Whatley.

The latest findings are not uniform across pollsters, and several battleground contests remain close in broader polling averages.

Trump's approval and voter priorities

The New York Times/Siena surveys found that just 38% of likely voters across the seven battleground states approved of Trump's job performance. Democratic candidates also led among independent voters in every state surveyed, while respondents expressed greater trust in Democrats on the cost of living, foreign wars and protecting the interests of ordinary people.

Across the seven states, Democratic candidates held a nine-point advantage over Republicans on handling the cost of living.

The findings are consistent with broader national dissatisfaction. An Associated Press-NORC survey conducted on October 8-12 found that 36% of voters approved of Trump's job performance, while 64% disapproved.

Also Read: Power bills and data centers cast rare spotlight on utilities in US midterms

The economy and cost of living emerged as the leading election concerns, cited as important voting issues by 85% and 84% of respondents, respectively. Health care followed at 69%, while 64% identified the war with Iran as an important issue.

The survey also found that 47% of voters wanted Democrats to control the House, compared with 38% who preferred Republicans. For the Senate, the figures were 46% and 38%, respectively.

What the polls cannot predict

Despite Democrats' polling advantage, uncertainties surrounding turnout and survey accuracy could affect the results.

The New York Times/Siena polls, which surveyed between 610 and 1,215 likely voters in each state, had margins of sampling error ranging from 3.3 to 4.8 percentage points. They also found that voters who made their decisions during the preceding month favoured Republicans by nine points, indicating that late shifts in support could matter.

Polling errors can arise from inaccurate turnout assumptions, difficulties reaching certain demographic groups and systematic biases shared by multiple surveys.

The surveys also found that Democrats' support among some key demographic groups had strengthened since September, although polling has historically struggled to accurately measure white working-class voters.

With several Senate contests separated by only a few percentage points, small differences between polling estimates and actual voting patterns could change the balance of power in Congress.

headline: 3 killed, at least 29 injured in shootings near US college communities
description: Gunfire reported in Indiana, Delaware, Alabama, Illinois and Colorado over weekend, prompting multiple investigations
author: Anadolu Agency
article_text:
Three people were killed and at least 29 others injured in a series of shootings near US college communities across five states over the weekend, Fox News reported on Sunday.

In Bloomington, Indiana, seven people were hospitalised after gunfire erupted near Indiana University's homecoming celebrations at around 1.30 am (01030PKT) on Sunday.

Police detained a man carrying a firearm and recovered a gun and shell casings. No fatalities were reported, and investigators have yet to determine whether the man fired any shots.

In Newark, Delaware, at least six people were hospitalised following a shooting Saturday night on Main Street near the University of Delaware.

Local police launched an investigation, while university President Laura Carlson urged the community to support the victims and witnesses.

"We are all impacted," she said.

In Birmingham, Alabama, one person was killed and eight others wounded near Legion Field following the Magic City Classic football game between Alabama A&M and Alabama State.

Nearly 70,000 fans attended the annual rivalry game, which Alabama A&M won 31-28.

Police detained one person for questioning and recovered multiple weapons.

In Bloomington, Illinois, a 19-year-old woman was killed, and seven others hospitalised after shots were fired near Illinois Wesleyan University shortly before 1.25 am Sunday.

Another woman remained in critical condition, while the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives joined the investigation.

In Boulder, Colorado, a shooting at a home in the University Hill neighbourhood left a 19-year-old University of Colorado Boulder student dead and another person critically injured.

Police believe the violence followed an attempted forced entry into the property after officers had earlier dispersed a large party.

headline: Tarar announces plans to revive PTV Drama, Film Academy
description: Information minister says project will be 'game-changer' as youth to get practical training in modern studios
author: Life And Style Desk
article_text:
Information Minister Attaullah Tarar on Monday announced plans to restore and modernise the Pakistan Television (PTV) Drama and Film Academy, aiming to equip young people with contemporary filmmaking and digital production skills.

In a statement shared on X, Tarar said he had chaired a meeting to discuss the restoration of the academy "and giving it a new shape."

The minister said that, for the first time in Pakistan, specialised training in colour grading would be made available locally, eliminating the need for aspiring professionals to travel abroad to acquire the skill.

Tarar added, "In collaboration with the private sector, we will provide practical training to the youth in modern studios for films, dramas, and digital content; we will also partner with universities, and PTV's revenue will increase."

The minister concluded with expressing hope that the project would "prove to be a game-changer."

The proposed revival of the PTV Drama and Film Academy came at a time when the film, television and digital content industries increasingly rely on advanced production techniques including colour grading, post-production and modern studio technologies.

By bringing specialised training facilities to Pakistan and involving private-sector partners and universities, the initiative aims to help bridge the skills gap and prepare a new generation of professionals for opportunities in the evolving media landscape.
