headline: Merub Ali praises Dananeer, Romaisa Khan for proving their talent beyond social media
description: Says digital platforms helped actors find opportunities in television that traditional routes might not have offered
author: Life And Style Desk
article_text:
Merub Ali has praised the growing presence of social media influencers in the entertainment industry, pointing to fellow actors Dananeer Mobeen and Romaisa Khan as examples of digital creators who have successfully made the transition to television.

In a recent interview, Ali spoke about how social media had helped introduce fresh talent to the entertainment industry, arguing that performers should be judged on their abilities rather than how they first gained public attention.

Speaking about Mobeen, Ali described her as a prime example of how social media could help talented newcomers find opportunities in showbiz.

“I just believe in talent. The perfect example of this is Dananeer and I am so happy that social media brought her here. Dananeer is so talented and if we did not have social media, it would be really difficult to navigate and find people like her,” she said.

Ali also praised Khan, who built a substantial online following through her social media content before establishing herself as a television actor.

“Romaisa is also a beautiful actress. I have seen her play various roles and her expressions and acting through her eyes. I don’t know how she does it. She is great and social media gave us that,” Ali said.

Her appreciation extended beyond their career transitions to the criticism they faced along the way. Recalling the reaction to Mobeen's casting in the popular drama Sinf-e-Aahan, Ali said some viewers had questioned whether an influencer could hold her own alongside established actors.

“During Sinf-e-Aahan, I remember people used to say that she is an influencer and you guys have let her get this far. She proved herself in that drama,” she recalled.

View this post on Instagram

Mobeen first rose to widespread attention in 2021 after her short video featuring the now-famous 'Pawri Ho Rahi Hai' line went viral. The clip became a social media phenomenon, spawning countless recreations and memes.

She subsequently made her television debut in Sinf-e-Aahan, playing Sidra alongside established actors including Sajal Aly, Yumna Zaidi, Kubra Khan, Syra Yousuf and Ramsha Khan. Despite initial questions surrounding her casting, Mobeen went on to establish herself as an emerging television performer.

Khan followed a similar path, using her online popularity and comedic personality as a springboard into mainstream entertainment.

She gradually moved into television, taking on different roles and demonstrating her acting abilities in projects such as Jinn Ki Shadi Unki Shadi and Dekh Zara Pyar Se. She is currently known for playing Hamna in Dar-e-Nijaat.

Interestingly, Ali's own career also connects her to the discussion. Before becoming a familiar face on television, she worked as a model and built a presence on social media. She made her television debut in the 2021 drama Sinf-e-Aahan, which introduced her to a wider audience, before appearing in projects including Paristan and Wabaal.

Ali is currently appearing in the drama Izzat as Rutba, alongside Atabik Mohsin and Hashaam Khan.

Having experienced her own transition into television, Ali's appreciation of Mobeen and Khan carries an added perspective. Her comments underline how digital platforms can help emerging performers find opportunities in an industry that has traditionally relied on established routes to discover talent.

For Ali, an influencer background should not determine whether someone deserves a place in showbiz. What ultimately matters is the ability to prove one's talent on screen.

headline: Vikings suffer first loss while Broncos edge Chiefs in NFL
description: Denver edge Kansas City 28-24 in a dramatic finish
author: AFP
article_text:
Minnesota became the last NFL club to tumble from the unbeaten ranks on Sunday while Denver made a game-ending defensive goal-line stand to deny Patrick Mahomes and edge Kansas City in a thriller. A dramatic day also saw Josh Allen make history in sparking Buffalo over injury-hit Baltimore, which might have lost quarterback Lamar Jackson for the rest of the season. Detroit's Jared Goff threw a seven-yard touchdown pass to Jameson Williams with 4:35 to play, giving the Lions a 19-15 victory over visiting Minnesota, which fell to 6-1. Kyler Murray threw an eight-yard touchdown pass to TJ Hockenson with 8:44 remaining and flipped a two-point conversion pass to Jordan Addison for a 15-12 Vikings lead only for Goff to deliver Detroit the victory. "Too much inconsistency. We didn't deliver at a high enough level," Murray said. "We had our opportunities to get it done. We just didn't." The Lions lost linebacker Jack Campbell to a frightening injury early in the fourth quarter. He was carted off the field and taken to a hospital, where the club said he will stay overnight for observation and evaluation. Denver rallied with two fourth-quarter touchdowns to defeat the visiting Chiefs 28-24, only the third loss for Mahomes in 83 games with a lead of 10 or more in the final period. Mahomes threw his third touchdown pass, a four-yard effort to Noah Gray, for a 24-13 lead. Bo Nix threw a touchdown pass and two-point conversion and Jonah Coleman had a five-yard touchdown run with 1:56 to play to put Denver ahead. The Chiefs (5-2) drove to the Broncos' one-yard line only for Mahomes to be sacked by Malcolm Roach on the final play. Denver's Nix completed 20 of 32 passes for 222 yards and two touchdowns. "I'm so proud of our team," he said. "It was a big win for us. I can't say enough about our team fighting. It's an awesome feeling." - Jackson hurt in loss - At Buffalo the Bills improved to 6-1 as Allen threw for 289 yards and two touchdowns and ran for another score in a 36-10 rout of the Ravens. Jackson, a two-time NFL Most Valuable Player who had missed the past three games with an ankle injury, suffered a right thumb injury on Baltimore's first play from scrimmage when, on a pass, his hand struck the hand of Buffalo linebacker Greg Rousseau. Jackson will require thumb surgery and be placed on injured reserve, potentially ending his season, Ravens coach Jesse Minter said. "That's a tough deal," Minter added. "We'll see where that's at." Reserve Tyler Huntley replaced Jackson only to suffer a foot injury that forced emergency quarterback Joe Fagnano into his first NFL game. "We'll figure out what we have and try to put together the best plan," said Minter, whose team play against Jacksonville on Thursday. Allen broke Jim Kelly's team record for career touchdown passes on an 11-yard connection to DJ Moore with 12:18 remaining and added a 23-yard TD throw to Dalton Kincaid. "To break the records, it's cool, but it's not just me," Allen said. "A lot of guys have put in the work to get me here."

Overtime thrillers

At Dallas, Chad Ryland kicked a 42-yard field goal in overtime to deliver Arizona a 33-30 victory, after he had missed a conversion that would have won the game in the dying seconds of regular time. Joe Burrow's nine-yard touchdown run gave the host Bengals a 43-36 overtime triumph over Tennessee. Burrow also threw for 462 yards and five touchdowns. Jaylen Warren ran for 143 yards and a touchdown to lead Pittsburgh's 27-6 home triumph over Cleveland. Tampa Bay became the first team since 1974 to have zero pass completions, but the Buccaneers still beat visiting Atlanta 16-0 in heavy rain. Jacksonville beat Indianapolis 42-7 while Las Vegas bested the New York Jets 38-33. Drake Maye led New England to a 24-19 victory at Miami while the Los Angeles Rams kept the Los Angeles Chargers winless with a 24-9 triumph. In the late game, the Washington Commanders beat NFC East rivals Philadelphia 27-10, subjecting the Eagles to their sixth straight loss.

headline: Israel maintains highest state of alert on eve of US midterm elections
description: Israeli-US security coordination reaches highest levels amid possible escalation with Iran, Israeli news website says
author: Anadolu Agency
article_text:
Israel remained on the highest state of military alert on Monday, a day before the United States midterm elections, amid concerns over a possible resumption of war with Iran, according to Israeli media.

Americans head to the polls Tuesday for midterm elections halfway through Republican President Donald Trump’s second term, with all 435 seats in the House of Representatives, 35 Senate seats and governorships in 36 states up for grabs, alongside thousands of local positions and ballot measures.

Trump has repeatedly pledged not to launch new strikes against Iran before the midterm elections, while suggesting that military operations could resume afterward, amid a continued US military buildup in the region and stalled diplomatic efforts.

According to Israeli media, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s government has been pushing for renewed strikes against Iran, ostensibly aimed at overthrowing its government, although Israeli officials acknowledge that the final decision rests with the White House.

Israeli news website Walla reported Monday that the military remained on high alert amid US and Israeli concerns that Iran could launch a surprise attack, either directly or through allied groups, against American interests in the region or Israel. The report said intelligence agencies fear Tehran could stage a large-scale military provocation that might influence the US midterm elections.

Walla said the Israeli military had intensified defensive and offensive preparations in recent weeks in coordination with US Central Command (CENTCOM) and the Pentagon.

Citing unnamed Israeli military officials, the website said security coordination between Israel and the US had reached its highest levels and that Israel would receive advance warning if Washington decided to attack Iran. However, Israeli military assessments suggest that the likelihood of a US preemptive strike before the midterm elections remains low, as Trump prefers to exhaust diplomatic negotiations and pressure before resorting to military action, according to the report.

Walla also said that more than 3,000 US troops were stationed in Israel, noting that no unusual increase in American military aircraft arrivals had been recorded over the past week, unlike the periods preceding previous escalations.

The report added that Israeli officials believe Tehran is seeking to buy time in negotiations with Washington, while disagreements persist over Iran’s nuclear program and ballistic missiles.

Concerns over renewed war

Tensions between Washington and Tehran have persisted since the US and Israel launched a war against Iran in February, followed by a ceasefire in April and renewed confrontations between the US and Iran in July.

The developments come amid warnings that Netanyahu could seek to push Washington toward another military confrontation with Tehran.

In an article published Sunday, Haaretz military analyst Amos Harel warned that Netanyahu might resort to military and political escalation to remain in power, using the Iranian issue and pressures surrounding the US midterm elections. Harel also warned against attempts by Netanyahu to persuade Washington to resume military operations despite lacking a domestic mandate to launch another war.

Israeli Channel 12 reported Sunday that Netanyahu had pressed Trump during a phone conversation to resume the war against Iran after the US midterm elections, while the American president preferred to give diplomacy another chance.

The heightened security alert also comes amid political uncertainty in Israel following last week’s parliamentary elections. Netanyahu’s bloc secured 53 seats in the 120-member Knesset, compared with 48 for opposition parties led by former army chief Gadi Eisenkot and 19 for Arab parties.

No bloc secured the 61 seats required to form a government, leaving Israel facing a political deadlock. The results have complicated efforts to form a governing coalition amid disagreements among opposition parties over whether to seek support from Arab parties.

headline: Aashir Wajahat sparks 'Parwarish' reunion speculation with Samar Jafri, Abul Hassan
description: Director Meesam Naqvi's appearance in the picture also fuels hopes of another collaboration among the familiar faces
author: Life And Style Desk
article_text:
Aashir Wajahat has fuelled speculation about a possible reunion of the Parwarish team after sharing a picture with fellow actors Samar Jafri and Abul Hassan, alongside the drama's director, Syed Meesam Naqvi.

Captioned simply, “The boys”, the picture has prompted excitement among Pakistani drama fans, with many hoping the familiar faces are preparing to reunite for another television project.

The possibility of seeing the group work together again has particularly caught viewers' attention given the success of Parwarish and the popularity of its young cast.

View this post on Instagram

Fans were quick to flood the comments section with excitement, with one user expressing disbelief at the prospect of seeing the three actors together in a drama directed by Meesam.

“SAMAR, AASHIR, ABUL IN A DRAMA THAT TOO DIRECTED BY MEESAM SIR? WHAT COULD BE GREATER THAN THIS ???!!!!” one fan exclaimed.

Others were already imagining the possibilities of the cast, with one fan suggesting, “If you cast all of them together cast Aina too”, referring to Aina Asif, who starred alongside Jafri in Parwarish.

The reactions reflect the enthusiasm surrounding the possibility of another collaboration between the actors and director, although no new project has been officially announced.

Jafri and Hassan previously appeared together in the hit drama Parwarish, which premiered in April 2025. Directed by Naqvi and written by Kiran Siddiqui, the series explored generational differences, family pressures, identity and the challenges of growing up.

Jafri played Wali Jahangir, a young musician struggling to pursue his dreams amid family expectations, while Hassan portrayed Sameer. The drama resonated with younger audiences through its portrayal of family relationships and the pressures faced by young people.

Naqvi has also directed projects such as Mayi Ri and Parwarish, earning recognition for his work with young performers. Aashir, meanwhile, has another connection to the director, having appeared in the drama Kafeel as Subuk.

Beyond their professional collaborations, Wajahat and Jafri share a longstanding friendship that has become a favourite talking point among their followers.

The two have grown up in the entertainment industry together, building careers across acting and music. Their friendship has also translated into several creative collaborations, including the song Aaja Chal Jhoomay from the 2024 film Daghabaaz Dil and their appearance together in the Eid comedy Na Baligh Afraad.

Earlier this year, the duo teased their second musical collaboration, Tum Na Ho, with a nostalgic childhood photograph that offered fans a glimpse of how far the two friends had come together. Their musical partnership has continued to attract attention, with both artists discussing songwriting, music culture and their creative approaches in interviews.

headline: Raye announces major London homecoming as BST Hyde Park headliner
description: The singer will perform on July 10, with tickets going on sale November 10
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Raye is set to headline BST Hyde Park in London next summer, marking a major homecoming performance for the award-winning British singer.

The musician will take to the stage on July 10, 2027, with rising star Sienna Spiro announced as the first supporting act. Organisers are expected to reveal additional performers ahead of the event, which forms part of the annual summer concert series.

Tickets for the show will go on sale at 10am local time on November 10, according to the announcement reported by Variety.

The performance comes after a significant year for Raye, who recently won the prestigious Mercury Prize for her second album, This Music May Contain Hope. Released earlier in 2026, the record followed her acclaimed 2023 debut, My 21st Century Blues, which helped establish her as one of the UK’s most prominent contemporary artists.

Raye began her career as a songwriter before stepping into the spotlight as a solo performer. Her achievements include six BRIT Awards, the Ivor Novello Award for songwriter of the year and three Grammy nominations.

Her latest album has also produced the popular single “Where Is My Husband!”, further expanding her success.

The BST Hyde Park appearance will bring Raye back to the city where her musical journey began. She is the second headliner announced for the 2027 edition, following American rock band Bon Jovi, who are scheduled to perform on June 24.

Spiro, 21, will join Raye after gaining attention for her debut album, Visitor, which became the UK’s biggest debut album of the year and received gold certification from the RIAA.

With further acts still to be announced, Raye’s headline performance is shaping up to be a major highlight of next summer’s London music calendar.

headline: Jack Lowden breaks silence on James Bond rumours as casting race heats up
description: The ‘Slow Horses’ star says he is grateful for the support but refuses to fuel speculation
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Jack Lowden has addressed speculation surrounding his potential casting as the next James Bond, calling the rumours flattering while making clear he does not intend to add to the ongoing conversation.

In an interview with British GQ, the Slow Horses actor responded to growing reports linking him to the iconic role, including public support from his co-star Gary Oldman.

“It is all very flattering. It is nice to be mentioned for any role, and I am just not really going to add to the noise,” Lowden said. He also described Oldman as a sweetheart, saying the praise was particularly lovely coming from someone he admired.

Lowden, who plays River Cartwright opposite Oldman in the Apple TV spy series, suggested that speculation about Bond often follows young male actors once they begin appearing in more traditionally suited roles.

“As a young male actor, generally, the minute you are not playing a zany artist type, the minute you are in a suit, people fling it at you,” he said.

His comments arrive amid reports that the search for Daniel Craig’s successor is approaching its final stages. Variety previously reported that Amazon MGM was preparing final screen tests, with Lowden and Callum Turner reportedly among the contenders. Josh O’Connor has also been linked to the process, alongside several other actors whose names have circulated in recent months.

Oldman fuelled interest in Lowden’s chances in September when he said he hoped his co-star would land the role. However, he later clarified that he had heard only a rumour about a shortlist and had no confirmed information about the casting decision.

The next Bond film will be directed by Denis Villeneuve, with Steven Knight writing the screenplay. Casting director Nina Gold is overseeing the search.

Craig last played Bond in No Time to Die in 2021. Amazon MGM has yet to announce his successor or confirm when the casting news will be revealed.

article_html:
Jack Lowden has addressed speculation surrounding his potential casting as the next James Bond, calling the rumours flattering while making clear he does not intend to add to the ongoing conversation.

In an interview with British GQ, the Slow Horses actor responded to growing reports linking him to the iconic role, including public support from his co-star Gary Oldman.

“It is all very flattering. It is nice to be mentioned for any role, and I am just not really going to add to the noise,” Lowden said. He also described Oldman as a sweetheart, saying the praise was particularly lovely coming from someone he admired.

Lowden, who plays River Cartwright opposite Oldman in the Apple TV spy series, suggested that speculation about Bond often follows young male actors once they begin appearing in more traditionally suited roles.

“As a young male actor, generally, the minute you are not playing a zany artist type, the minute you are in a suit, people fling it at you,” he said.

His comments arrive amid reports that the search for Daniel Craig’s successor is approaching its final stages. Variety previously reported that Amazon MGM was preparing final screen tests, with Lowden and Callum Turner reportedly among the contenders. Josh O’Connor has also been linked to the process, alongside several other actors whose names have circulated in recent months.

Oldman fuelled interest in Lowden’s chances in September when he said he hoped his co-star would land the role. However, he later clarified that he had heard only a rumour about a shortlist and had no confirmed information about the casting decision.

The next Bond film will be directed by Denis Villeneuve, with Steven Knight writing the screenplay. Casting director Nina Gold is overseeing the search.

Craig last played Bond in No Time to Die in 2021. Amazon MGM has yet to announce his successor or confirm when the casting news will be revealed.

headline: Jordan’s king calls Israel's expansionist ambitions ‘biggest threat’ to region’s future
description: King Abdullah II says regional security, stability depend on Palestinians securing their rights
author: Anadolu Agency
article_text:
Jordan’s King Abdullah II said on Monday that Israel’s expansionist ambitions pose the greatest threat to the region’s future, stressing that regional security and stability cannot be achieved without Palestinians securing their rights to their land.

“Israeli expansionist ambitions remain the greatest threat to the region’s future and its hopes,” Abdullah said in a speech to parliament.

He pointed to the continuing humanitarian catastrophe in the Gaza Strip and Israeli attacks in the occupied West Bank, including East Jerusalem, despite international calls to halt Israeli violations.

He stressed that there could be no security or stability in the region without recognising the Palestinian people’s rights to their land.

“Those who believe tyranny grants legitimacy are mistaken, and those who believe time erases the truth are mistaken,” the king said.

He reaffirmed Jordan’s commitment to its principles, Arab identity and defending Arab causes, pledging to maintain that position as his father had before him and his son would after him.

The monarch also stressed that achieving a unified Arab position would remain a priority for Jordan.

Israel has waged a genocidal war on Gaza since October 2023, killing more than 74,000 Palestinians and injuring over 175,000 others, most of them women and children.

Israeli military operations and attacks by illegal occupiers have also intensified in the occupied West Bank, including East Jerusalem.

headline: Miley Cyrus reportedly considers acting career as she weighs her next move
description: Miley Cyrus is reportedly exploring acting opportunities while prioritising her sobriety and long-term career plans
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Miley Cyrus is reportedly reconsidering the direction of her career, with an insider claiming that the singer is exploring a possible return to acting while deciding what she wants from her future.

Speaking to the Daily Mail, the source said Cyrus was uncertain about her next steps following her recent musical projects and October performances at the Hollywood Bowl.

"She's struggling with what comes next," the insider said. "Miley is at a point in her life where she's really trying to figure out who she is and, more importantly, what she wants to be beyond just being Miley Cyrus, the celebrity."

The source also suggested that her latest music had not achieved the success she had hoped for. "Her new music hasn't really taken off the way she wanted," they said.

Cyrus released "Bass Persuades" in September before performing two sold-out shows at the Hollywood Bowl in October. The performances featured new material, familiar hits and a tribute to her late godmother, Dolly Parton.

According to the insider, Cyrus is considering acting as a way to demonstrate a different side of her abilities. "One thing she's been considering is getting back into acting, because she wants the opportunity to show people there's more to her than the Miley Cyrus persona they've known for years," the source said.

Her previous acting credits include The Last Song, LOL, So Undercover and the Black Mirror episode "Rachel, Jack and Ashley Too". However, the insider claimed that finding a suitable project has been difficult, adding that Cyrus wants a serious film or television role.

The singer has also spoken openly about prioritising her sobriety. In a May 2025 interview, she said, "The sobriety is like, that's like my God. I need it, I live for it. I mean that it's changed my entire life."

Cyrus previously explained that touring made maintaining her sobriety difficult, helping shape her reluctance to return to an extensive touring schedule.

The insider also suggested that Parton's death has been particularly difficult for Cyrus, as the country singer had been a source of advice and guidance throughout her life.

According to the source, Cyrus is now trying to find her own direction while considering what comes next professionally.

headline: Israeli forces fire tear gas at Palestinian students, teachers in West Bank as occupiers block roads
description: Israeli army, occupiers carry out 3,133 attacks last month in 52.8% increase from previous month, commission says
author: Anadolu Agency
article_text:
Dozens of Palestinian students and teachers suffered suffocation from Israeli tear gas on Monday, as occupiers blocked several roads in the latest escalation in the occupied West Bank.

In the village of Al-Mughayyir, east of Ramallah, Israeli forces fired tear gas canisters toward a school, leaving dozens of students and teachers suffering from suffocation, village council head Amin Abu Aliya told Anadolu. Medical teams treated those affected at the scene, while Palestinian Civil Defence crews worked to clear tear gas from classrooms, he said.

The village has been subjected to repeated attacks by Israeli forces and occupiers in recent weeks, Abu Aliya said.

Separately, Israeli occupiers blocked several roads used by Palestinian vehicles in the northern Salfit governorate, according to local sources. The occupiers closed a road near the towns of Haris and Kifl Haris, as well as the Wadi Qana road linking Salfit and Qalqilya governorates, and set tires on fire along a main road, they said.

Israeli occupiers also used stones to block a road leading to Al-Zaytoonah University of Science and Technology in the Wadi al-Shaer area, disrupting traffic.

Meanwhile, occupiers stole around 90 goats in the Salhab area of the northern Jordan Valley, according to Mutaz Bisharat, an official responsible for monitoring settlement building in Tubas and the Jordan Valley. “The theft came amid an increase in attacks by Israeli occupiers against Palestinians and their property across the West Bank,” Bisharat said.

Earlier Monday, the Palestinian Colonisation and Wall Resistance Commission said Israeli occupiers carried out 1,369 attacks across the West Bank in October, up 111.6% from 647 in September. The commission said the Israeli army and occupiers carried out a combined 3,133 attacks last month, a 52.8% increase from the previous month. Israeli forces were responsible for 1,764 of the attacks.

Nearly 750,000 Israeli occupiers live in 156 illegal settlements and around 360 outposts across the West Bank, including East Jerusalem, according to Palestinian figures.

In June, 14 United Nations special rapporteurs warned that the sharp rise in violence by Israeli occupiers, with state support and complicity, posed an existential threat to Palestinian communities.

Arrests

In another development, the Israeli army arrested six Palestinians during raids in Nablus, Ramallah and Hebron, according to the Palestinian Prisoners Media Office.

In Nablus, Israeli forces arrested a Palestinian from the town of Tell and rearrested journalist Samer Khuwaira after raiding his home in Nablus city. Khuwaira had previously been detained on April 10, 2025, and placed under administrative detention without charge later that month. He spent about nine months in Israeli prisons before being released on Jan. 7, 2026.

In Ramallah, Israeli forces arrested two young men during a raid on Kobar village and another Palestinian from Al-Amari refugee camp. Another Palestinian was arrested after Israeli forces raided his home in Dura, south of Hebron.

Israeli military operations and occupier attacks have intensified across the West Bank since the start of Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza in October 2023. More than 1,220 Palestinians have been killed and around 13,350 wounded in the West Bank during that period, while more than 26,000 have been arrested, according to Palestinian figures.

headline: Hilary Duff reveals she was ‘f***ing done’ with Lizzie McGuire after show ended
description: The singer says she struggled to establish her identity beyond the Disney character after becoming a household name
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Hilary Duff has opened up about feeling exhausted by her Lizzie McGuire fame after the hit Disney Channel series ended, admitting she once wanted nothing to do with the character or its most famous song.

In an interview with Paper magazine, Duff reflected on filming The Lizzie McGuire Movie, which followed the television series and featured the memorable track “What Dreams Are Made Of”.

The singer said the demanding production schedule had taken a toll on her. She filmed 30 episodes during one year and another 35 the following year, while her growing popularity meant audiences increasingly identified her exclusively with Lizzie.

“I was pretty done with Lizzie at that time,” Duff said, explaining that she wanted people to recognise her as an individual rather than constantly associate her with the Disney character.

The experience also affected her relationship with “What Dreams Are Made Of”. Duff recalled reaching a point when she felt she would never perform the song again, partly because she did not own it and wanted to move beyond her television persona.

However, her perspective has changed over time. Duff recently re-recorded the track for her *(Mine)* EP and performed it live for the first time during her Small Rooms, Big Nerves Tour.

She said singing it now feels different because she can appreciate what the song means to fans while also embracing it as part of her own musical history.

Duff also admitted that looking back, she would welcome the opportunity to revisit parts of that period. Although she remains grateful that audiences connected with the show and film, she said she was not fully comfortable with the experience at the time.

Lizzie McGuire premiered in January 2001 and ran for two seasons, ending in 2004 after 65 episodes. The film helped cement the character’s lasting place in pop culture.

headline: Savannah Guthrie makes emotional plea for answers as mother Nancy remains missing
description: Nancy disappeared from her Tucson, Arizona, home after reportedly being last seen at around 9:30pm on January 31
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Savannah Guthrie has made another emotional public appeal for information about her missing mother, Nancy Guthrie, saying her family cannot move forward without answers.

The Today show presenter shared a photograph of an old drawing made by her 12-year-old daughter, Vale, on Instagram on Sunday, November 1, 2026.

The drawing featured a blue umbrella and the handwritten message: “I know it might not seem like it, but I really need my mommy.”

Reflecting on the illustration, Savannah wrote: “Found this old drawing from my daughter today. It says so much about how I feel. The world goes on, things appear ‘normal’ — as we try to keep going and be strong, especially for our young kids — but it’s not and it never will be.”

View this post on Instagram

The 54-year-old journalist said her family continues to ache for Nancy, 84, and desperately wants information about her whereabouts.

“We cannot move forward,” she wrote. “We need someone to help us, tell us what you know.”

Savannah also described her mother as “a light in this world” and appealed to the public to help bring her home.

“We want to celebrate her and give her the dignity she deserves,” she added. “The reward is still available. Please. We are begging you. Please help us.”

Nancy disappeared from her Tucson, Arizona, home after reportedly being last seen at around 9:30pm on January 31.

The FBI subsequently released footage showing a masked individual outside her property.

The family is offering a $1 million reward for information leading to Nancy. Several alleged ransom notes have also emerged during the investigation.

Savannah previously acknowledged the possibility that her mother might no longer be alive, while emphasising that the family still needs answers and wants her home.

headline: Matt Damon and David Letterman make brief cameos in 'The Gilded Age' season 4 premiere
description: Matt Damon and David Letterman appear briefly in opening episode of 'The Gilded Age’s' fourth season
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Matt Damon and David Letterman made unexpected appearances in the season four premiere of HBO’s The Gilded Age, although viewers could easily have missed their brief cameos.

The pair appear at approximately eight minutes and 33 seconds into the episode, crossing a street together without speaking.

Damon wears a top hat, an ascot, a long coat and distinctive sideburns with a moustache, while Letterman appears in a bowler hat and an all-black outfit, retaining his familiar beard.

Neither actor has any dialogue, and their appearance is limited to the short scene. Their presence is one of several surprises in the season premiere, which also introduces significant developments for the show's central characters.

Among the episode's major storylines is the wedding of Oscar van Rhijn (Blake Ritson) and Enid Turner (Kelley Curran). The pair enter a lavender marriage, which appears to be a mutually understood arrangement.

Enid later reveals to Agnes van Rhijn (Christine Baranski) that both she and Oscar entered the marriage fully aware of his sexuality. She also expresses her intention to support his interests in the arts and Agnes' charitable work.

Meanwhile, Marian (Louisa Jacobson) reunites with her former fiancé Larry Russell (Harry Richardson) at an after-hours gathering following the wedding.

After an incident forces them to take shelter at a hotel, the former couple spend the night together. Marian becomes concerned about the potential damage to her reputation the following morning.

Elsewhere, Peggy celebrates the publication of her book, while her future mother-in-law, Elizabeth Kirkland (Phylicia Rashad), appears to have plans involving her and her mother.

In another major development, Gladys (Taissa Farmiga) survives a life-threatening childbirth emergency, but undergoes a hysterectomy to save her life.

New episodes of The Gilded Age season four air on Sunday nights at 9pm ET/PT on HBO.

headline: PM Shehbaz directs SBP, FBR to resolve tax issues faced by SMEs, exporters
description: Calls for comprehensive risk-coverage mechanism to make it easier for businesses to obtain loans
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Monday directed the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) and the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) to work together to resolve tax-related issues faced by Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises (SMEs) and exporters, as part of efforts to expand access to financing for priority sectors, the Prime Minister's Office (PMO) said.

According to a statement issued by the PMO, the prime minister, chairing a meeting to review lending facilities for SMEs, housing and agriculture, directed the Finance Ministry to address financing-related problems faced by stakeholders in these sectors and formulate a comprehensive strategy.

He called for a comprehensive risk-coverage mechanism to make it easier for small and medium-sized businesses to obtain loans.

PM Shehbaz said the development of SMEs, housing and agriculture was among the government's foremost priorities, as these sectors could support economic growth and create employment opportunities for young people.

He praised banks that had performed well in extending loans to the three priority sectors under government initiatives. However, he directed the SBP and finance ministry not to extend concessions to banks that were slow in providing financing to farmers, SMEs and beneficiaries of the Prime Minister's Apna Ghar Scheme.

"Banks are of key importance for the development of the private sector," he said, adding that he expected them to extend the same cooperation in financing priority sectors as the government and its institutions provided to banks.

The prime minister said SMEs had significant potential to contribute to economic growth, promote exports and create employment opportunities. He described agriculture as the backbone of the national economy and said the government was working to increase exports through value addition of agricultural produce.

He added that the Apna Ghar Scheme would promote several industries linked to the housing and construction sectors.

The PMO said that during the meeting, officials briefed the prime minister that the SBP was working on three main pillars to increase lending to priority sectors: improving regulations, sharing risks and costs between the government and banks, and expanding digital facilities.

As part of these efforts, the SBP had recently launched the SME Connect digital portal, which allows business owners to apply for loans and track the progress of their applications.

The meeting was informed that, as of October 23, loans worth Rs511 billion had been approved under the Prime Minister's Apna Ghar Programme, covering 86,899 applications. Loans amounting to Rs91 billion had been disbursed to 15,584 applicants, the PMO said.

The total volume of housing finance had reached Rs455 billion, benefiting 187,317 borrowers. In the agriculture sector, lending had reached Rs1,329 billion, benefiting approximately 3.5 million people. Meanwhile, SME financing had reached Rs1,148 billion, with 342,458 businesses receiving loans.

The government had set a target of increasing lending to both the agriculture and SME sectors to Rs1,500 billion by the end of fiscal year 2027, officials said.

The meeting was also informed that the government had introduced risk-sharing and credit-guarantee measures for the housing, agriculture and SME sectors. Work was underway to simplify loan procedures, reduce documentation requirements and improve access to financing through digital systems.

Officials also presented performance indicators for commercial banks across the three priority sectors. The prime minister praised banks that had demonstrated good performance.

Federal ministers Ahsan Iqbal, Rana Tanveer Hussain, Dr Musadik Malik, Mian Riaz Hussain Pirzada, Muhammad Aurangzeb, Attaullah Tarar and Shaza Fatima Khawaja attended the meeting, along with the Prime Minister's Adviser Haroon Akhtar, Minister of State Bilal Azhar Kiani, SBP Governor Jameel Ahmad, MNAs Hafizuddin and Chaudhry Iftikhar Nazir, and senior officials. Heads and representatives of leading commercial banks were also present.

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Monday directed the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) and the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) to work together to resolve tax-related issues faced by Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises (SMEs) and exporters, as part of efforts to expand access to financing for priority sectors, the Prime Minister's Office (PMO) said.

According to a statement issued by the PMO, the prime minister, chairing a meeting to review lending facilities for SMEs, housing and agriculture, directed the Finance Ministry to address financing-related problems faced by stakeholders in these sectors and formulate a comprehensive strategy.

He called for a comprehensive risk-coverage mechanism to make it easier for small and medium-sized businesses to obtain loans.

PM Shehbaz said the development of SMEs, housing and agriculture was among the government's foremost priorities, as these sectors could support economic growth and create employment opportunities for young people.

He praised banks that had performed well in extending loans to the three priority sectors under government initiatives. However, he directed the SBP and finance ministry not to extend concessions to banks that were slow in providing financing to farmers, SMEs and beneficiaries of the Prime Minister's Apna Ghar Scheme.

"Banks are of key importance for the development of the private sector," he said, adding that he expected them to extend the same cooperation in financing priority sectors as the government and its institutions provided to banks.

The prime minister said SMEs had significant potential to contribute to economic growth, promote exports and create employment opportunities. He described agriculture as the backbone of the national economy and said the government was working to increase exports through value addition of agricultural produce.

He added that the Apna Ghar Scheme would promote several industries linked to the housing and construction sectors.

The PMO said that during the meeting, officials briefed the prime minister that the SBP was working on three main pillars to increase lending to priority sectors: improving regulations, sharing risks and costs between the government and banks, and expanding digital facilities.

As part of these efforts, the SBP had recently launched the SME Connect digital portal, which allows business owners to apply for loans and track the progress of their applications.

The meeting was informed that, as of October 23, loans worth Rs511 billion had been approved under the Prime Minister's Apna Ghar Programme, covering 86,899 applications. Loans amounting to Rs91 billion had been disbursed to 15,584 applicants, the PMO said.

The total volume of housing finance had reached Rs455 billion, benefiting 187,317 borrowers. In the agriculture sector, lending had reached Rs1,329 billion, benefiting approximately 3.5 million people. Meanwhile, SME financing had reached Rs1,148 billion, with 342,458 businesses receiving loans.

The government had set a target of increasing lending to both the agriculture and SME sectors to Rs1,500 billion by the end of fiscal year 2027, officials said.

The meeting was also informed that the government had introduced risk-sharing and credit-guarantee measures for the housing, agriculture and SME sectors. Work was underway to simplify loan procedures, reduce documentation requirements and improve access to financing through digital systems.

Officials also presented performance indicators for commercial banks across the three priority sectors. The prime minister praised banks that had demonstrated good performance.

Federal ministers Ahsan Iqbal, Rana Tanveer Hussain, Dr Musadik Malik, Mian Riaz Hussain Pirzada, Muhammad Aurangzeb, Attaullah Tarar and Shaza Fatima Khawaja attended the meeting, along with the Prime Minister's Adviser Haroon Akhtar, Minister of State Bilal Azhar Kiani, SBP Governor Jameel Ahmad, MNAs Hafizuddin and Chaudhry Iftikhar Nazir, and senior officials. Heads and representatives of leading commercial banks were also present.

headline: Gigi Hadid surprises Bollywood fans by revealing her love for 'Kabhi Khushi Kabhie Gham'
description: Supermodel shares her appreciation after Neelam Kaur Gill recreates Kareena Kapoor's iconic Poo look for Halloween
author: Life And Style Desk
article_text:
American supermodel Gigi Hadid gave Bollywood fans an unexpected reason to celebrate after revealing her love for the 2001 blockbuster Kabhi Khushi Kabhie Gham (K3G).

The revelation came after British fashion model Neelam Kaur Gill paid tribute to one of Bollywood's most recognisable style icons by dressing up as Kareena Kapoor Khan's character, Pooja Sharma, popularly known as Poo, for Halloween.

View this post on Instagram

Gill recreated Poo's instantly recognisable fashion aesthetic, sporting a pink crop top, mini skirt and signature accessories that brought back memories of the character's iconic looks.

Sharing the outfit on Instagram, Gill captioned her post, "Tell me how it was” living my 2000’s Bollywood fantasy courtesy of the QUEEN Kareena Kapoor in K3G".

However, it was Hadid's response that particularly caught the attention of fans. The supermodel joined the conversation by commenting, “I love this movie,” revealing her appreciation for the popular Hindi film.

Gill was equally delighted by the unexpected endorsement from the international fashion star. Responding to Hadid, the model wrote, “@gigihadid truly the best ever <3”.

The exchange prompted several amused reactions from fans, with one Instagram user admitting that Hadid's appreciation for the film was something they had never anticipated.

Hadid's appreciation for Bollywood also brings an interesting connection to South Asian culture into the conversation. The supermodel was previously in a relationship with British singer Zayn Malik, with whom she shares a daughter, Khai.

Malik has Pakistani roots through his father, Yaser Malik, who is British-Pakistani, while his mother, Trisha Malik, has English and Irish heritage.

Hadid and Malik have previously spoken about raising their daughter with an understanding of her multicultural background. In a 2021 interview with Elle, Hadid discussed the importance of helping Khai appreciate the different cultural identities she inherits from both sides of her family.

Although Hadid has not linked her love for Kabhi Khushi Kabhie Gham to her personal connections with South Asia, her comment has delighted Bollywood fans, who are enjoying the unexpected crossover between international fashion and Hindi cinema.

headline: James McAvoy reveals movie that continues to earn him 'bonkers' royalties
description: James McAvoy says 2016 horror film 'Split' remains his most consistent source of residual income
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
James McAvoy has revealed that Split, the 2016 psychological horror film directed by M. Night Shyamalan, continues to earn him regular residual payments nearly a decade after its release.

The actor, 47, played a man with dissociative identity disorder in the film, which was produced by Blumhouse Productions. Made on a reported budget of $9 million (£6.7 million), Split went on to gross $278 million (£207 million) worldwide, becoming a major commercial success.

Speaking on the Happy Sad Confused podcast, McAvoy explained that although actors sometimes receive small residual cheques from previous projects, Split is the one film that consistently generates payments for him.

"You get the odd cheque for, you know, a couple 100 quid here or sometimes you get checks for, like, 25 cents and you're like, 'It literally costs more to post this than it did for me to cash it,'" he said. "But the only one that really consistently pays me is Split."

McAvoy also recalled the film's financial performance shortly after its release, describing how quickly it began generating returns.

"I think it was made for like $6 million or something like that? And let's say they spent 30 advertising it. In our first weekend, we made 40, so we were in profit," he said. "Our first residual cheque came at the end of the first weekend. It was bonkers."

The actor also discussed what he learned from working with Shyamalan on Split and its sequel, Glass. He credited the filmmaker's preparation and ability to communicate his plans effectively with the crew.

"The thing I took away from him is his preparedness," McAvoy said, explaining that Shyamalan made both films on modest budgets while carefully maximising shooting time and resources.

headline: AI models mostly smarter than top scientists, OpenAI's Altman says
description: CEO says AI models capable of performing white-collar work but people must 'remain in control of the future'
author: Anadolu Agency
article_text:
Advanced artificial intelligence (AI) models have progressed to become mostly smarter than the brightest scientists and capable of performing significant portions of white-collar work, OpenAI Chief Executive Sam Altman said on Monday.

Speaking at the opening ceremony of the Abu Dhabi International Petroleum Exhibition and Conference in the United Arab Emirates, Altman highlighted the dramatic leap in AI capabilities over the past year. "At the start of this year, AI was mostly not as smart as our smartest scientist, and now it's mostly smarter than them," Altman said.

"AI was mostly not able to do a lot of white-collar jobs, and now it mostly can do a lot of parts of that," he added.

Altman stressed that despite the disruptive impact on global economies and employment, human judgement, creativity and accountability must remain central to the technology's deployment. "We think it is absolutely critical that people remain in control of the future; there should not be a handoff to AI, there should not be a gradual 'we are going to let AI decide what is best for us,'" he said.

"AI needs to be a tool built for people and needs to serve people, not the other way around," Altman noted.

Addressing concerns surrounding the massive electricity demands of computing infrastructure, he described physical power supply as the single biggest bottleneck for the sector. "Everything else we're going to make huge progress on, except atoms are still atoms and the physical world that has to power this is going to be the dominant factor of the cost and the abundance," he said.

Altman also noted that global per capita token consumption has surged from near zero six years ago to roughly 100,000 tokens a month, while top institutional users consume about 500 billion tokens monthly.

headline: Curry Barker wants to release extended cut of horror hit ‘Obsession’ with 20 minutes of unseen footage
description: The filmmaker says the longer version is separate from the theatrical film’s director’s cut
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Curry Barker has revealed that a longer version of his horror film Obsession exists and that he hopes to release it in the near future.

Speaking to Rolling Stone, the filmmaker said the extended edition runs approximately 20 minutes longer than the theatrical release. The film currently has a runtime of 108 minutes, meaning the additional footage could bring the alternative version close to two hours and 10 minutes.

Barker was careful to distinguish the longer edition from the film’s director’s cut, describing the theatrical version as the definitive director’s cut. The version he hopes to release would instead be an extended cut featuring additional material.

“I would say that there’s a longer version of the movie that I would love to release, for sure,” Barker said.

The announcement has sparked interest among viewers curious about what was left out of the final edit. However, Barker has not confirmed a release date or explained how the additional scenes would change the finished film.

Obsession marked a major breakthrough for Barker, who previously built an audience through comedy and sketch videos on YouTube before moving into feature filmmaking. The horror project was reportedly filmed in just 20 days on a budget of approximately $750,000.

Its commercial performance helped establish Barker as a filmmaker to watch, while also generating discussion about the possibility of a sequel.

Barker is also attached to a reboot of the Texas Chainsaw Massacre franchise. His next feature, Anything But Ghosts, is expected to come before that project.

For now, the extended edition remains a possibility rather than a confirmed release. Barker has expressed interest in making the additional footage available, but further details about its distribution have yet to be announced.

headline: Kelly Osbourne reportedly hurt after Sharon and Jack meet estranged sister Aimee
description: Kelly Osbourne is reportedly upset after Sharon and Jack met with her estranged sister shortly before her birthday
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Kelly Osbourne was reportedly hurt after her mother, Sharon Osbourne, and brother, Jack Osbourne, met with her estranged older sister, Aimee, shortly before Kelly's 42nd birthday.

According to unnamed sources quoted by The Sun, the meeting took place on October 26 outside Jack's Los Angeles home.

Photographs reportedly showed Jack, 40, hugging Aimee, 43, while Sharon was also present. Kelly was not pictured at the gathering.

The sources claimed Kelly was surprised by the meeting but respected her family's right to maintain relationships with Aimee.

They added that she would not allow the visit to affect her relationships with her mother or brother. The report suggested Sharon and Jack had reached out to support Aimee following the death of their father, Ozzy Osbourne, in July 2025.

A source claimed Aimee had withdrawn while grieving and found photographs and videos of her father difficult to watch.

The reported meeting comes weeks after Kelly discussed her estrangement from Aimee during a September 15 appearance on Paul C.

Brunson's We Need to Talk podcast. She explained that Aimee had largely kept to herself during their childhood, while Kelly and Jack developed a closer relationship.

Kelly also discussed feeling that her older sister had been embarrassed by the family, although she acknowledged she could not speak for Aimee. Asked whether reconciliation was possible, Kelly said, "I respect her. I accept her. But we're different. And that's OK."

The Sun's report suggested Kelly might be open to hearing from Aimee if she made the first move, although this was attributed to a source rather than a new public statement from Kelly.

Jack previously described his relationship with Aimee as distant, saying in July 2025: "We're not close at all."

Aimee has also spoken about her decision not to appear on the family's MTV reality series, The Osbournes, explaining in a 2015 interview that she wanted to protect her privacy.

headline: Taylor Swift reveals childhood habit her husband Travis Kelce has to tolerate
description: Taylor Swift shares long-running inside joke she still enjoys with childhood friend Abigail Anderson
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Taylor Swift has revealed that she still shares an unusual childhood tradition with her best friend, Abigail Anderson Berard, more than two decades after they first met, and it is something their husbands have learnt to tolerate.

The singer discussed the habit during a Toy Story 5 screening and question-and-answer session in New York City on Sunday, November 1.

Speaking alongside filmmaker Andrew Stanton, Swift explained how the film's portrayal of friendship reminded her of her longstanding relationship with Abigail.

The pair met when Swift moved to Nashville at the age of 14 and started at a new school. They soon discovered a shared love of impersonating characters from the 2004 comedy Napoleon Dynamite.

Their running joke has continued into adulthood, with the two still speaking to each other in voices from the film.

"We still do this," Taylor admitted. "It's something our husbands have to put up with."

The comment was also a reference to Swift's husband, Kansas City Chiefs player Travis Kelce. Abigail married Charles Berard in 2022.

Their friendship has previously influenced Swift's music. Abigail inspired the singer's 2008 song "Fifteen", from her album Fearless, which reflects on the experiences of starting high school. She also appeared in the track's music video.

Abigail has remained part of Swift's life as her career has developed, accompanying her to the 2015 Grammy Awards and appearing in the 2020 Netflix documentary Miss Americana. Swift also celebrated when her friend welcomed her first child in 2024.

Swift attended Sunday's event to discuss Toy Story 5, for which she co-wrote and produced the song "I Knew It, I Knew You" with Jack Antonoff. The track was inspired by Jessie, the cowgirl character introduced in Toy Story 2.

Reflecting on the film's friendship themes, Swift said, "That hit me so hard watching the film."

The singer discussed the habit during a Toy Story 5 screening and question-and-answer session in New York City on Sunday, November 1.

Speaking alongside filmmaker Andrew Stanton, Swift explained how the film's portrayal of friendship reminded her of her longstanding relationship with Abigail.

The pair met when Swift moved to Nashville at the age of 14 and started at a new school. They soon discovered a shared love of impersonating characters from the 2004 comedy Napoleon Dynamite.

Their running joke has continued into adulthood, with the two still speaking to each other in voices from the film.

"We still do this," Taylor admitted. "It's something our husbands have to put up with."

The comment was also a reference to Swift's husband, Kansas City Chiefs player Travis Kelce. Abigail married Charles Berard in 2022.

Abigail has remained part of Swift's life as her career has developed, accompanying her to the 2015 Grammy Awards and appearing in the 2020 Netflix documentary Miss Americana. Swift also celebrated when her friend welcomed her first child in 2024.

headline: Michael Jackson’s ‘Thriller’ breaks streaming record with 6.6m Halloween streams reaching Global Spotify No. 1
description: The 1982 hit more than doubled its daily streams as Halloween listeners sent it soaring up the charts
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Michael Jackson has secured another remarkable milestone as his iconic song Thriller reached the top of Spotify’s Global chart for the first time since its release in 1982.

The legendary Halloween anthem claimed the No. 1 position on October 31, recording an impressive 6.606 million streams worldwide. The achievement came almost 44 years after the song first captivated audiences, demonstrating its enduring appeal across generations.

The streaming surge was closely tied to Halloween celebrations, with listeners returning to the classic track as part of the season’s musical traditions. Its daily streams more than doubled from October 30, when Thriller received 3.09 million plays and ranked at No. 8 on the Global chart.

The milestone also followed another major achievement for the song, which reportedly reached No. 1 on Apple Music’s US chart during the same Halloween period. Together, the results highlight the continued popularity of Jackson’s music across major streaming platforms.

The latest chart success marks Jackson’s second Global Spotify No. 1 in 2026. His song “Billie Jean” previously returned to the summit in June, adding another significant moment to the late singer’s enduring musical legacy.

Thriller also experienced renewed success on the Billboard Hot 100 following Halloween celebrations last year, when it returned to the chart’s top 10. Its latest streaming performance could offer further momentum for its position on the next chart update.

Originally released in 1982, Thriller remains one of Jackson’s most recognisable songs.

headline: Suki Waterhouse adresses secret Robert Pattinson marriage rumours
description: Suki Waterhouse and Robert Pattinson are considering 'massive' wedding after busy year, amid secret event rumours
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Suki Waterhouse has confirmed that she and Robert Pattinson have not married yet, putting an end to speculation that the couple secretly tied the knot. However, the singer and actress has hinted that they could eventually celebrate with a large wedding.

In an interview with The Sunday Times, published on November 1, Waterhouse, 34, discussed her plans with Pattinson, 40, explaining that they have considered holding a substantial celebration rather than opting for a small ceremony.

"It would either be all or nothing," she said of their wedding. "If we were going to go for it we'd have a massive party, blow it out."

Waterhouse added that their wedding plans are currently on hold until after the end of the year because of their demanding work schedules.

Rumours that the couple had already married began in January 2025, when actress Sharon Stone referred to Pattinson as Waterhouse's "husband".

The comment prompted speculation that the pair had secretly exchanged vows, although Waterhouse has now clarified that they are still engaged.

The couple began dating in 2018 and have been together for nearly a decade. Reflecting on their relationship, Waterhouse spoke about how happy she feels with Pattinson.

"It is almost a decade and that is a beautiful thing," she shared. "It's a thing that I go, 'I can't believe I have this in my life and I can't believe that I'm so happy.'"

The couple also share a two-year-old daughter, who was born in March 2024. Waterhouse said she feels confident about their approach to parenting, despite describing their circumstances as an "abnormal life".

"I feel good about how we're doing it and we are both just so connected to her," she said. "She's such a wonderful, happy girl."

headline: Sydney Sweeney backed by former Bond girl for potential role in next 007 film
description: Trina Parks says Sydney Sweeney has qualities to become next leading lady in James Bond franchise
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Sydney Sweeney has received support from a former James Bond actress as speculation continues over the future of the long-running film franchise and its next leading man.

Trina Parks, who played Thumper opposite Sean Connery in the 1971 film Diamonds Are Forever, has said Sweeney would make a suitable Bond girl in the upcoming era of 007. Parks made history as the first Black actress to portray a Bond girl in the series.

Speaking to The Telegraph, Parks praised Sweeney's acting range, confidence and screen presence, suggesting that her approach to her public image would suit the franchise's changing portrayal of female characters.

"She has done quite a range of acting things and basically has got ownership of her sexual identity," she said. "Not only is she a talented actress, but has this Hollywood classic kind of style and poise, which really works for her projects and brand."

Parks also discussed how the role of women in Bond films has evolved, arguing that modern audiences expect female characters to have greater independence.

"I feel for modern cinema and film-making and the future of Bond, audiences want to see a woman opposite Bond who is independent and has ownership of her sexuality — Sydney has those qualities," she added.

The comments come as producers reportedly begin the search for Daniel Craig's successor following his departure from the franchise in 2021's No Time To Die.

Actors Callum Turner and Jack Lowden have been linked to the final audition stages, although no replacement has been officially confirmed.

Producers Barbara Broccoli and Michael G. Wilson are reportedly considering a significant reinvention of the franchise for a new generation.

Speaking to The Telegraph, Parks praised Sweeney's acting range, confidence and screen presence, suggesting that her approach to her public image would suit the franchise's changing portrayal of female characters.

"She has done quite a range of acting things and basically has got ownership of her sexual identity," she said. "Not only is she a talented actress, but has this Hollywood classic kind of style and poise, which really works for her projects and brand."

Parks also discussed how the role of women in Bond films has evolved, arguing that modern audiences expect female characters to have greater independence.

"I feel for modern cinema and film-making and the future of Bond, audiences want to see a woman opposite Bond who is independent and has ownership of her sexuality — Sydney has those qualities," she added.

The comments come as producers reportedly begin the search for Daniel Craig's successor following his departure from the franchise in 2021's No Time To Die.

Actors Callum Turner and Jack Lowden have been linked to the final audition stages, although no replacement has been officially confirmed.

Producers Barbara Broccoli and Michael G. Wilson are reportedly considering a significant reinvention of the franchise for a new generation.

headline: Candice Swanepoel sparks Tom Brady engagement rumours after being spotted with mysterious ring
description: The sighting sparked buzz about the model and the NFL star taking their reported relationship to the next level
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Tom Brady and Candice Swanepoel have fuelled engagement speculation after the supermodel was photographed wearing a gold band on her left ring finger in Florida.

The 37-year-old Victoria’s Secret Angel was spotted in Surfside, Florida, in late October 2026, wearing the jewellery with an all-black outfit.

The sighting prompted questions about whether the model and the retired NFL star had taken their reported relationship to the next level.

However, there is currently no confirmed engagement, and neither Brady nor Swanepoel has publicly acknowledged being a couple.

According to reports, the ring could simply be a personal jewellery choice, with no evidence linking it to a proposal.

Dating rumours involving the pair first emerged through Us Weekly and were subsequently reported by People.

Sources cited by TMZ claimed their relationship began in June, with the two reportedly favouring private locations around Miami.

Swanepoel, a South African supermodel, became internationally recognised through her work with Victoria’s Secret. She also founded sustainable swimwear brand Tropic of C in 2018.

She shares two sons, Anacan and Ariel, with her former fiancé, Hermann Nicoli. The pair ended their relationship in 2018 after more than a decade together.

Meanwhile, Page Six reported alleged tension between Swanepoel and fellow model Joan Smalls, who was previously linked to Brady.

“She and Joan share a longstanding history and a friendship that Candice will always respect,” Swanepoel’s representative told Us Weekly.

For now, the engagement rumours remain unconfirmed, with the gold ring offering no definitive indication of a proposal.

headline: Warriors continue unbeaten streak
description: Muneeba Ali’s side register a comfortable 24-run win over team Champions
author: Sports Desk
article_text:
Muneeba Ali’s Warriors registered their third consecutive win the PCB Women’s Super-3 T20 Tournament as they beat Tuba Hassan’s Champions by 24 runs in the fifth match here at the Iqbal Stadium, Faisalabad on Monday.

Chasing a target of 155 runs, Champions were dismissed for 130 in 19.2 overs with left-arm spinner Ayesha Bilal taking four for 15. Warriors have now won three matches on the trot and will face Incredibles in their fourth match on Tuesday.

Incredibles have lost all of their three matches and are out of the race for the final as the Champions have managed two wins out of their four matches and have secured the berth.

On Monday, Ayesha showcased her prowess with the ball as she cut through Champions’ batting by taking wickets of Saira Jabeen, Najiha Alvi and Tuba (18, 16b, 2x4s) at a time when the game would have easily tilted away. Ayesha later pinned no.10 Tayyaba Imdad leg-before to return figures of 4-0-15-4.

Warriors’ spinners Zunash Abdul Sattar and Rameen Shamim also contributed as the former picked up 2-27 with her leg-spin and the latter 1-17 including the wicket of the aggressive opener Komal Khan (18, 12b, 2x4s, 1x6).

Natalia Parvaiz (31, 27b, 2x4s, 1x6) and Shawaal Zulfiqar (22, 12b, 3x4s, 1x6) were the two other batters who showed some resistance, striking boundaries regularly but couldn’t convert their innings. Pacer Diana Baig picked up two wickets, while Humna Bilal dismissed Shawaal.

Earlier, Champions inserted Warriors in after winning the toss. No.4 Hafsa Khalid (47, 36b, 5x4s, 2x6s) and no.6 Rameen (29, 24b, 4x4s) rescued the Warriors’ innings with a 65-run stand after they were 66-4. Diana put the finishing touch towards the end as she contributed valuable 19 runs off 14 balls hitting two fours and one six.

For Champion, Tayyaba picked up two wickets, Tuba, Momina Riasat, Fatima Khan and Ayesha Rehman dismissed one batter each. Tuba had also run out Hafsa as Warriors posted 154-8 in 20 overs.

Scores in brief

Match 5 – Warriors beat Champions by 24 runs at Iqbal Stadium, Faisalabad

Warriors 154-8, 20 overs (Hafsa Khalid 47, Rameen Shamim 29, Sadaf Shamas 22, Diana Baig 19; Tayyaba Imdad 2-27)

Champions 130 all out, 19.2 overs (Natalia Parvaiz 31, Shawaal Zulfiqar 22; Ayesha Bilal 4-15, Diana Baig 2-19, Zunash Abdul Sattar 2-27)

Player of the match – Ayesha Bilal (Warriors)

description: 20-year-old scores 185 runs in five matches ODI tri-series

article_text:
Pakistan’s emerging wicketkeeper-batter Saad Baig says he is determined to turn promising starts into bigger scores and establish himself as a dependable performer after an encouraging debut ODI series.

The 20-year-old scored 185 runs in five matches during the recently concluded tri-nation series, including his maiden half-century, and helped Pakistan defeat Sri Lanka by three wickets in Saturday’s final at Lahore’s Gaddafi Stadium.

Baig made 74 in the title-deciding match as Pakistan chased down a target of 326 to lift the trophy. He also took three catches behind the stumps during the tournament.

Speaking on the Pakistan Cricket Board’s digital programme Straight Drive with Salman Butt, Baig reflected on his first international series, adapting to different batting positions and managing pressure situations.

“My plan was simple. I wanted to carry the confidence and belief I had developed in domestic cricket into international cricket,” he said.

“Whatever the situation, whether early wickets had fallen or a partnership was developing, I wanted to back my skills, play my natural game and trust my abilities.”

Baig said he also learned the importance of adjusting his approach according to the match situation.

“Sometimes you have to control your natural instincts and build a partnership according to the situation. I tried to do that while communicating with my batting partner,” he said. “I am thankful to have contributed to the team’s success.”

The left-hander progressed through Pakistan’s age-group system, representing the country at under-13, under-16 and under-19 levels before captaining the side at the 2024 ICC Men’s Under-19 World Cup.

Pakistan reached the semi-finals of that tournament, losing to Australia by one wicket.

Baig said making the transition from age-group cricket to the senior national team was particularly rewarding, especially as several members of his under-19 batch have also reached the international level.

“It is a very good feeling to have come through a proper pathway, from age-group cricket to captaining Pakistan in the U19 World Cup and then representing the senior national side,” he said.

“I am grateful to have made a positive start, but this is only the beginning. My focus is to keep learning, identify areas where I can improve and develop my game further so that I can perform consistently for Pakistan.”

headline: Oil refineries to bear Rs15b burden to ease fuel price pressure leading to Rs15 cut in petrol price
description: Petroleum minister says a Pakistani-bound LNG cargo ship was attacked before it entered the Strait of Hormuz
author: Web Desk
article_text:
The government on Monday announced that oil refineries would bear a burden of Rs15 billion per month, which would allow petrol to be sold Rs15 cheaper than it was in the global market amid the US-Israeli war on Iran.

In a press conference in Islamabad, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik, speaking alongside Information Minister Attaullah Tarar, noted that the international market, reacting to the tensions in the region, was witnessing an upward trend, adding that the spot market and Platts rates had been demonstrating fluctuations, but petrol prices were also governed by other factors.

Malik said: “Oil refineries were requested to take a step to support the public during this difficult time, and I am glad that they listened to us … the Rs15 increase that was coming in the petrol prices on Friday, they helped the government with that, and because of that we were able to maintain the price".

He stated that the impact of the Rs15 per litre burden shifting from consumers to oil refineries had already been "passed in Friday’s price determination".

Malik said that further improvement would be seen by the public, expressing his gratitude to the refineries for standing with the government to provide assistance to the public during difficult times.

“I am grateful to all the refineries that saw the public is in difficulty and with the government’s help … increased their throughput,” the minister said.

The petroleum minister underscored that the government did not intend to cause "hardship" to any stakeholder and wanted to navigate the international crisis through a "transparent process".

"The oil refineries' three-month profits are even more than their annual profits from last year," Malik stated.

Talking about the PSO tenders, Malik stated that the “premium” saw an increase of around $10-20.

He said that before the crisis, the premium of the refineries was $5 per barrel, and even today a $20 limit had been established, adding that the government would have to step in and protect the public in case of further difficulties.

Malik further noted that insurance costs had risen manifold, and there are even more issues related to logistics.

He added: “Logistics have a cost. A very large crude carrier that was once available for a few hundreds of thousands of dollars is now rarely available for even a million dollars.”

"In this purview, a couple of PSO tenders were issued that underscored an extreme excess under premium, which records several factors," he added.

Speaking about Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif's approach to providing relief to consumers, Malik said the government was providing relief to the people according to its means.

Apart from the fuel relief scheme that was offering "targeted relief" to 13 million people, the government had undertaken several other measures to alleviate the burden on the masses, the petroleum minister stated.

The minister underlined that the government tried to improve its procurement operations by optimising costs, but the difficult situation in the region was affecting this measure, further adding that this was reflected in the petroleum pricing mechanism outlined before October 31, which included a premium of $20.

To a question regarding a delay in finalising 16 to 22 LNG cargoes to meet winter needs, Malik said that the "premier and a few friends had a view that the difference between the Qatar LNG and the one bought from the open market was high".

Tarar added that the fuel-subsidy scheme for motorcyclists and car owners would continue, noting that so far Rs27 billion had been disbursed under the scheme and 15 million beneficiaries had registered for it.

Attack on Pakistani-bound LNG cargo ship

Malik also stated that a Pakistani-bound LNG cargo ship was attacked before it entered the Strait of Hormuz without naming the culprits.

“The LNG ship was hit before it entered the Strait of Hormuz”, he said during the press conference.

While speaking on the attack, Tarar said that the government would share only the verified information, urging people to avoid any speculation about the perpetrators.

While responding to a question about how the ship was attacked when Pakistan had secured clearance from Iran, the information minister stated that there were "no shortages of supplies", further noting that "it is a sensitive time and one should avoid speculation."

Qatar and Saudi Arabia had earlier condemned the attack on the LNG tanker, calling it a “dangerous act” that threatened the security of global energy supplies. Pakistan had negotiated with Iran to secure safe passage for the LNG carrier, Al Mayeda,

Qatar's foreign ministry on Sunday said it had initiated the necessary investigations to determine the circumstances of the incident and identify those responsible for the attack on the vessel.

Revision in petrol pricing mechanism

The federal government on Friday revised the petrol pricing mechanism, directing refineries to surrender the difference between import and ex-refinery prices as a petroleum levy, with the resulting benefit to be passed on to consumers through a corresponding reduction in petrol prices.

Under the revised arrangement, petrol's import price would be determined on the basis of the actual import cost of the relevant Pakistan State Oil (PSO) cargo. If the actual import cost was unavailable for a particular day's pricing, the premium, incidentals and customs duty of the last available cargo might be used.

For the next 30 days, refineries would be entitled to an ex-refinery price calculated by fixing the premium, incidentals and customs duty at the levels applicable on March 7, 2026, before the war.

Ex-refinery price is the rate at which an oil refinery sells petroleum products to oil marketing companies before the addition of government taxes, duties, dealer commissions and other distribution costs.

Under the arrangement, the difference between the import price and the ex-refinery price would have to be surrendered by refineries under the petroleum levy head of account C03901. The resulting benefit would be passed on to petrol consumers exclusively through a corresponding reduction in the retail price.

The Petroleum Division had directed all oil refineries to deposit the differential amounts in accordance with the OGRA price and petroleum levy notifications issued from time to time. Refineries would also be required to submit daily reports of domestic petrol sales, along with computerised payment receipts and challans, to the Petroleum Division and OGRA for verification and reconciliation.
