If the actual import cost was unavailable for a particular day's pricing, the premium, incidentals and customs duty of the last available cargo might be used.

For the next 30 days, refineries would be entitled to an ex-refinery price calculated by fixing the premium, incidentals and customs duty at the levels applicable on March 7, 2026, before the war.

Ex-refinery price is the rate at which an oil refinery sells petroleum products to oil marketing companies before the addition of government taxes, duties, dealer commissions and other distribution costs.

Under the arrangement, the difference between the import price and the ex-refinery price would have to be surrendered by refineries under the petroleum levy head of account C03901. The resulting benefit would be passed on to petrol consumers exclusively through a corresponding reduction in the retail price.

The Petroleum Division had directed all oil refineries to deposit the differential amounts in accordance with the OGRA price and petroleum levy notifications issued from time to time. Refineries would also be required to submit daily reports of domestic petrol sales, along with computerised payment receipts and challans, to the Petroleum Division and OGRA for verification and reconciliation.

headline: Adrian Hamilton-Manns formally takes charge as PIA's new CEO
description: Airline says Hamilton-Manns brings over 30 years of experience and expertise in restructuring and reviving airlines
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Adrian Hamilton-Manns has formally assumed charge as the new chief executive officer (CEO) of Pakistan International Airlines (PIA), bringing three decades of commercial aviation experience to the national flag carrier.

"PIA's board is pleased to announce the appointment of Hamilton-Manns as the CEO. He brings a wealth of leadership & strategic experience, and his appointment marks a pivotal chapter in PIA’s ongoing transformation," the airline said in a statement posted on X on Monday.

The statement added that Hamilton-Manns had previously served as CEO of three airlines and held leadership positions at several others. With more than 30 years of professional experience, he is regarded by the airline as an expert in restructuring and reviving aviation businesses.

The PIA consortium and board also expressed appreciation for the services of outgoing CEO Air Vice Marshal (AVM) Amir Hayat, acknowledging his leadership during a period of significant challenges for the airline.

According to the airline, PIA navigated difficult circumstances during Hayat's tenure, including operational and regulatory challenges.

The airline credited the outgoing CEO with overseeing significant improvements in aviation safety standards, helping secure the lifting of restrictions on PIA flights to Europe and the United Kingdom, and preparing the organisation for privatisation.

The board acknowledged Hayat's contribution to the airline's efforts to restore international operations and strengthen its institutional position.

Last year in December, the government sold its 75% stake in PIA for Rs10.1 billion cash to a consortium, marking the completion of the first major privatisation transaction in two decades by offloading the white elephant.

The consortium of Habib, Fawad Ahmed Mukhtar, Gohar Ejaz and Aqeel Karim Dhedhi — Pakistan's renowned businesspersons- placed the highest bid of Rs135 billion for the 75% shares in the 13th round of open auction. It beat another cash-rich consortium led by Muhammad Ali Tabba.

Later in June, the Arif Habib Consortium took over PIA management as govt formally completed the privatisation process.

headline: Britney Spears accuses family of mistreatment and says she will find a new family
description: The singer says she was prevented from holding her niece during visits in the pandemic
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Britney Spears has made fresh allegations about her family, claiming that she was treated unfairly during visits to Louisiana and felt as though she had been made to feel like a slave.

In an Instagram caption published on November 2, the singer accused her younger sister, Jamie Lynn Spears, and former husband Kevin Federline of actions that left her feeling hurt. She ended the post with a pointed statement: “I will find a new family.”

View this post on Instagram

Spears alleged that Jamie Lynn never allowed her to hold her niece, Ivey Joan Watson, during visits that she described as two week stays in Louisiana during the COVID-19 pandemic. She also claimed Federline would not let her use the bathroom when she visited the house to collect their sons, Sean Preston and Jayden James.

The singer did not provide specific dates or further details about the alleged incidents. Her claims have not been independently verified, and neither allegation should be treated as an established account of what happened.

Her comments have renewed attention on an earlier message from December 28, 2025, when Spears addressed her niece publicly and wrote that she wanted to hold her. However, that post does not independently confirm her latest allegation.

The family tensions also come against the background of Spears’ long running dispute over her conservatorship, which began in 2008 and ended in November 2021. Her father, Jamie Spears, had overseen her estate for much of that period.

In her 2023 memoir, The Woman in Me, Spears expressed affection for Jamie Lynn and her family, writing that she would always love her sister.

In an Instagram caption published on November 2, the singer accused her younger sister, Jamie Lynn Spears, and former husband Kevin Federline of actions that left her feeling hurt. She ended the post with a pointed statement: “I will find a new family.”

She also claimed Federline would not let her use the bathroom when she visited the house to collect their sons, Sean Preston and Jayden James.

The singer did not provide specific dates or further details about the alleged incidents. Her claims have not been independently verified, and neither allegation should be treated as an established account of what happened.

headline: Islamabad court sentences man to 7-year jail term for filming objectionable video of teenage boy
description: Judge says the convict will have to serve an additional six months in prison in case of non-payment of the fine
author: Fiaz Mahmood
article_text:
An Islamabad Additional District and Sessions Court sentenced Raja Haris Naveed to seven years of rigorous imprisonment in a cybercrime case involving the harassment of a 16-year-old boy and the recording of an objectionable video without his consent, it emerged on Monday.

Additional District and Sessions Judge Muhammad Afzal Majoka announced the verdict after finding the main accused in the case “guilty”, according to the order dated October 29.

The accused was convicted under Section 22 (child pornography) of the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act (PECA), 2016, read with Sections 34 (acts done by several persons in furtherance of common intention) and 109 (Punishment of abetment if the Act abetted committed in consequence and where no express provision is made for its punishment) of the Pakistan Penal Code, 1860.

The court also imposed a fine of Rs1 million on the convict under the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act (PECA) amended in 2025.

In case of non-payment of the fine, the judge said the convict will have to serve an additional six months in prison.

According to the case details, the accused lured a 16-year-old matriculation student into a drawing room and confined him. He then threatened and harassed the minor at gunpoint before recording an objectionable video without his consent.

The court acquitted co-accused Shahzaib Miraj, granting him the benefit of the doubt, as the prosecution failed to establish his involvement in aiding or abetting the crime.

In a similar case, an Islamabad court on October 22 sentenced two men to 10 years in prison each for blackmailing a 12-year-old girl and sharing her objectionable pictures.

Judge Majoka awarded each convict seven years' imprisonment and a fine of Rs1 million under Section 22 of PECA.

Under Section 24 (cyber stalking) of the same act, both convicts were sentenced to an additional three years in prison each and fined Rs1 million each, bringing their total prison term to 10 years each and the fine to Rs2 million each.

The case was registered by the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency on the complaint of the minor girl's father, according to The Express Tribune.

headline: Hayley Atwell reveals Marvel filmed multiple Peggy Carter storylines for ‘Avengers: Doomsday‘
description: The actress discussed her return while promoting her new MGM+ series ‘Treasure Island’
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Hayley Atwell has revealed that Marvel Studios filmed several different storylines for Peggy Carter in the upcoming Avengers: Doomsday, although some versions did not make the final cut.

The actress, who has portrayed Peggy Carter across multiple Marvel projects, discussed her return while promoting her new MGM+ series Treasure Island.

Speaking alongside co-star David Oyelowo on The Playlist’s Bingeworthy podcast, Atwell offered an insight into the film’s production process.

“We tried different things, we shot different things,” she explained, confirming that Marvel explored multiple creative directions for her character.

Atwell indicated that some storylines received further development, while others were eventually abandoned as the filmmakers worked towards the final version.

She also expressed confidence in the studio’s approach, describing the upcoming film as an ambitious project with considerable attention to audience expectations.

Directed by Anthony and Joe Russo, Avengers: Doomsday is scheduled to arrive in cinemas on December 18,2026.

The film will bring together characters from different Marvel timelines and universes, although its central storyline remains largely undisclosed.

Atwell’s return was first reported by Deadline in December 2024 before Marvel officially confirmed her involvement at San Diego Comic-Con in 2026.

However, the studio has yet to reveal whether she will portray the original Peggy Carter or the Captain Carter variant.

The character’s previous appearances include Captain America: The First Avenger, Agent Carter, What If…? and Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness.

With Avengers: Secret Wars scheduled for December 17, 2027, Peggy’s role could prove important to Marvel’s continuing multiverse storyline.

Atwell’s comments suggest audiences may ultimately see a version of the character shaped by several different creative approaches.

headline: Junaid Khan calls for greater investment in independent music, diverse TV stories
description: Actor-musician says Pakistani TV needs more male-centred narratives, greater room for action and crime genres
author: Life And Style Desk
article_text:
Actor and musician Junaid Khan believes Pakistan's entertainment industry needs to move beyond its established commercial formulas, arguing that independent music deserves greater investment and television needs to make room for stories beyond its predominantly female-centred programming.

From the decline of dedicated music channels to the lack of male-centred narratives on television, Khan believes there is considerable room for the industry to diversify. He is particularly interested in exploring action and crime-based projects, genres he feels deserve greater representation in Pakistani entertainment.

In a conversation with Atiqa Odho, Khan discussed his journey across music and acting, the emergence of independent musicians, the commercial priorities shaping television content and his aspirations to move into production.

Khan believes Pakistan's music industry has enormous potential, particularly with the emergence of younger artists and the accessibility of digital platforms. However, he feels the industry has not invested enough in creating independent opportunities for musicians.

"Now music is played more on YouTube so brands invest those into their dramas," he explained, pointing to the shift in how music is consumed and commercially supported. "I think most of our channel heads invest music in drama because that is where the money is. If needed, they could have invested in a music channel," he added.

He recalled how dedicated music channels once provided artists with an important platform before the availability of free Indian music and copyright-related challenges contributed to their decline.

For Khan, music should not have to depend on a drama's popularity to attract investment. Dedicated music channels, independent productions, music videos and live performances could give musicians more opportunities to build their careers.

"The future of music in Pakistan is very bright," he said, adding, "There are so many artists, post-Spotify. So many kids in our homes make music on their computers and now they have a free stream platform."

He is particularly encouraged by younger musicians experimenting with sounds and genres rather than limiting themselves to conventional styles. "Kids these days make such good music and are very creative. There are different genres, not just classic," he said.

Khan also praised Young Stunners and Hasan Raheem. "Young Stunners are very good. Hasan Raheem is very interesting and has a good tone. There are many who are doing good and keep coming." He believes Pakistani music has also reached international audiences, while Karachi's concert culture has grown considerably since his early days performing live.

His concerns about commercial investment extend to television, where he believes audience demographics have a considerable influence on the stories broadcasters choose to finance.

Khan acknowledged that television research points towards a predominantly female audience, which influences the industry's programming decisions.

"TV is a female-centred audience, that is what research says. Women see it more," he said. He explained that broadcasters tend to prioritise the larger audience segment rather than invest in content aimed at smaller demographics.

While female-centred dramas have an established audience and an important place in Pakistani television, Khan's observations point to an opportunity to explore a wider range of experiences and genres.

Action, crime and thrillers, in particular, are areas he would like to see receive more attention. "I like action and crime. As a guy, that is where my interest lies despite it being difficult," he said.

Having spent considerable time in front of the camera, Khan is also interested in moving towards content creation and production. "I have produced a couple of my own music videos but want to start on television," he revealed.

His career across music and acting, however, was not necessarily the result of a carefully laid-out plan. Khan described himself as someone who has always needed to stay occupied, rather than someone who consciously set out to develop multiple talents.

"I have never thought of myself to be a man of multiple talents. I did not see talent that way. I always wanted to be doing something in life. I hated being free. I want to keep myself occupied," he added.

Recalling his college years, he said he was balancing education, employment and music. "I was studying, working, and then going for jams later in the night. Then life went in a way where I stayed like that. There was never a time when I was just free."

For Khan, music and acting have served different creative purposes. "Music for me was a mode of expression. With acting, I wanted to explore human scripts and minds. How people do these things and how actors work. I was interested in that from the very beginning," he said.

His interest in performance also extended to theatre. When Odho suggested he would be suited to musical theatre, Khan agreed, recalling watching Chicago in Pakistan and attending Broadway productions in New York. "I salute actors in Pakistan working in theatre," he added.

Away from his professional commitments, Khan also discussed the importance of balancing work, fitness and family life. He has two children, aged 12 and seven, and makes a conscious effort to dedicate time to them.

"I make sure that I give certain times in the day to family such as dropping kids to school. I then start my day early, go to gym, and go to work. I try to work five days a week and take at least Saturday or Sunday off. There should be balance in everything from fitness, work life, to family life," he said.

He also spoke candidly about the challenges fame can bring to married life, particularly when an artist receives attention from fans. "Salute to all the wives. Media wives are challenged by this. Even if they are aware if my man is next to me or close to me, they will always have that feeling that your partner is loved by others. That is a thing to bear."

Khan believes maintaining a healthy relationship requires involving one's partner in professional life while also respecting personal boundaries. "I try to involve myself and also distance. The plus and minus factor. Involve yourself but keep distance and don't let small issues make an impact," he said.

He added that he makes a conscious effort to leave his on-screen persona behind when returning home, ensuring that the pressures and attention associated with fame do not affect his family.

headline: Senior Communist Party official appreciates 'momentum' in Pakistan-China exchanges
description: Reiterates Beijing's commitment to further deepening its longstanding friendship with Pakistan
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Senior Chinese official Liu Haixing on Monday appreciated the ongoing momentum in high-level and party-to-party exchanges between Islamabad and Beijing, saying the engagements would further strengthen the longstanding friendship between the two countries.

The minister of the International Department of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China (IDCPC) expressed these views during a meeting with Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif at the PM House in Islamabad, where the two sides discussed bilateral relations as well as regional and international developments.

According to a statement issued by the PM Office, Haixing underscored the importance of continued high-level engagement and inter-party cooperation in further consolidating bilateral ties.

The Chinese official conveyed the greetings of his country’s leadership and reiterated Beijing's commitment to further deepening its longstanding friendship with Pakistan.

Welcoming the Chinese official and his delegation, the prime minister said, “Pakistan and China enjoy an ironclad, time-tested and All-Weather Strategic Cooperative partnership.”

PM Shehbaz also underscored that Pakistan-China friendship was anchored in mutual trust, mutual respect and deep-rooted bonds between the peoples of both countries.

He also appreciated the role of the IDCPC in promoting institutional linkages and cooperation between the political leadership of the two countries, while emphasising the importance of sustained political engagement and inter-party exchanges to bolster ties.

Reaffirming Pakistan's commitment to working closely with Beijing, the prime minister highlighted the shared focus on expanding cooperation in trade, investment, connectivity, infrastructure development, information technology and agricultural modernisation.

The prime minister later hosted a banquet in honour of the visiting Chinese dignitary and his delegation.

Meeting with CDF Munir

Earlier today, Haixing called on Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir at the General Headquarters in Rawalpindi, according to the military’s media wing.

The Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said in a statement, “During the meeting, both sides discussed matters of mutual interest, evolving regional and international security dynamics and bilateral relations,” adding that the two officials expressed their shared resolve to further strengthen the all-weather strategic cooperative partnership between Islamabad and Beijing.

It further underscored that during the meeting with the IDCPC minister, CDF Munir highlighted the historic and time-tested bonds between the two countries.

He also emphasised the importance of sustained high-level engagement, stronger institutional linkages and expanded cooperation across areas of mutual interest.

The ISPR said the visiting dignitary appreciated Pakistan’s contributions to regional peace and stability and expressed confidence in further advancing the longstanding strategic partnership between Pakistan and China.

The visit also coincides with the 75th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between Pakistan and China. The two countries established diplomatic ties on May 21, 1951, and have since expanded their cooperation across political, economic, diplomatic and security domains.

DPM Dar highlights political consensus in Pakistan for stronger Sino-Pak ties

Deputy PM and Foreign Minister Mohammad Ishaq Dar also highlighted the broad-based political consensus in Pakistan supporting the longstanding friendship with China, according to a statement issued by the Foreign Office.

DPM Dar said this while co-chairing the Symposium on Xi Jinping Thought on Party Building and Seminar on China-Pakistan Governance in Islamabad alongside Haixing.

Addressing the gathering, the deputy PM underscored the vital role of political parties in effective governance, institution-building as well as national development.

In his keynote address, Haixing thanked Pakistan's leadership for its continued efforts to promote political goodwill, saying such engagement played an important role in furthering bilateral cooperation.

Haixing's maiden visit to Pakistan reflects Beijing's push to deepen ties beyond conventional government-to-government diplomacy.

The IDCPC, which Haixing heads, serves as Beijing's principal channel for party-to-party diplomacy, maintaining links with ruling and opposition political parties and facilitating exchanges on governance, development and international affairs.

In May this year, PM Shehbaz's visit to China culminated in a renewed commitment by both countries to deepen their partnership, maintain high-level exchanges and strengthen defence and security cooperation under the 2025-2029 action plan.

Defence cooperation has remained a key pillar of bilateral relations.

During CDF Munir's visit to Beijing in July 2025, he held meetings with senior Chinese political and military leadership, including Vice President Han Zheng and officials of the People's Liberation Army.

Discussions covered defence and security cooperation, counterterrorism collaboration, joint training, defence modernisation and stronger institutional linkages.

Both sides also reaffirmed their commitment to expanding military-to-military cooperation and promoting regional peace and stability.

headline: Republicans, Democrats make midterm closing arguments as Michigan rift roils Senate race
description: Control of either chamber will constrain Trump's ability to pass legislation, empower Democrats to investigate
author: Reuters
article_text:
Democrats sought to contain a rift in Michigan's US Senate race after one of their own crossed party lines to endorse the Republican, while President Donald Trump pressed his legal efforts on Monday to ​intervene in ballot-counting as both parties made their closing arguments a day before midterm elections that will determine control of Congress.

Over a fast-moving weekend, US Representative Haley Stevens, who lost the Michigan Democratic Senate primary to Abdul ‌El-Sayed in a bitter contest, suddenly switched to backing Republican Mike Rogers and appeared with him at a Detroit church. The race is critical to Democrats' hopes of ending the 53-47 Senate majority held by Trump's Republicans in Tuesday's vote.

Stevens' Sunday surprise came the same day a federal judge dismissed a US Justice Department lawsuit seeking to block certification of election results in Alaska if Republican incumbent Senator Dan Sullivan narrowly loses in the battleground state.

An undeterred Trump, who has been holding daily rallies around the country for Republican candidates, filed an emergency request with the US Supreme ​Court on Monday to temporarily block California from counting mail-in ballots from more than 20,000 registered voters who federal officials allege are likely non-US citizens.

California said the lawsuit could disenfranchise 20,000 voters based on vague accusations and that ​the administration's process for identifying noncitizens was flawed and prone to error.

The president, who continues to falsely claim that his loss to Joe Biden in 2020 was caused by widespread ⁠fraud, was due to deliver remarks at 2 pm ET (1900 GMT) at the belated reopening of Washington's Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool. An earlier renovation as part of his beautification efforts for the US capital was botched by contractors, leading to the "American ​flag blue" liner peeling away, which Trump had wrongly blamed on vandals.

A spokesperson for El-Sayed's campaign said it raised $2.4 million on Sunday, its largest single-day fundraising haul, fueled by small-dollar donations averaging $36.74 from more than 65,000 donors.

Nonpartisan analysts generally favour Democrats' chances ​of winning a majority in the House of Representatives. Winning control of the Senate will be trickier, with those analysts now seeing races in traditionally Republican-leaning states including Texas, Kansas and Iowa as competitive for the opposition party, giving it more options for a path to the majority.

Control of either chamber would constrain Trump's ability to pass legislation and empower Democrats to investigate his administration, while a Senate majority would also allow them to block his appointees to federal courts, including the Supreme Court.

According to the University of Florida Election Lab, 55 million votes have been ​cast in person and by mail already, more than the 45 million cast in the 2022 midterm elections.

Michigan rift

Stevens called on El-Sayed to condemn an outside group's ad that she said blames Israel for high grocery prices.

"That ad was very painful," ​Stevens told CNN on Sunday night. "There are so many Democrats who want to vote for our Democratic nominee, and they're just being told, 'Hey, this is a party you don't belong in, or this is a campaign you don't belong in.'"

El-Sayed rejected Stevens' demand, saying she ‌was creating ⁠a distraction by revisiting a primary election she lost months prior.

"You guys love to play the condemn game," he told reporters on Saturday when asked about Stevens' demand. "I've already been clear that that ad was not made by me, and I do not agree with the contents of that ad."

El-Sayed, an Egyptian American Muslim born in Michigan, has been targeted by Trump and other Republicans who have repeatedly questioned his loyalty to the US and baselessly called him a terrorist sympathiser whose election would invite attacks on Americans. El-Sayed has called questions about his loyalty to the US "shameful".

The verbal attacks fit a broader pattern of inflammatory rhetoric from some Republicans targeting Arab Americans, Muslims and transgender people and portraying Democrats as communists and dangerous radicals ahead of the ​midterms.

Stevens' mother, Maria Marcotte, said her daughter decided to endorse ​Rogers because of what she described as dangerous political ⁠rhetoric from El-Sayed, pointing in part to his past appearances with Hasan Piker, a left-wing streamer who has been criticised for his comments about Israel and American Jews.

"She's really reached a point where she felt like her constituents, the people that she cares about, and the people she knows and loves are scared and frightened by some rhetoric that's coming out," Marcotte said ​in an interview with Reuters from the porch of her home in Birmingham, a northern Detroit suburb.

Democratic voter Pamela Johnson, 72, criticised Stevens after casting her ballot for El-Sayed ​in Warren, a Detroit suburb: "Haley Stevens ⁠is a traitor."

The Trump administration's attempt to intervene in Alaska's Senate race faltered when a federal judge dismissed the US Justice Department's lawsuit on Sunday that sought to block certification of the results if Republican incumbent Senator Dan Sullivan narrowly loses.

The Justice Department argued voters may be confused by the presence of a challenger named Daniel Sullivan Jr on the same ballot.

Over a fast-moving weekend, US Representative Haley Stevens, who lost the Michigan Democratic Senate primary to Abdul ‌El-Sayed in a bitter contest, suddenly switched to backing Republican Mike Rogers and appeared with him at a Detroit church. The race is critical to Democrats' hopes of ending the 53-47 Senate majority held by Trump's Republicans in Tuesday's vote.

Stevens' Sunday surprise came the same day a federal judge dismissed a US Justice Department lawsuit seeking to block certification of election results in Alaska if Republican incumbent Senator Dan Sullivan narrowly loses in the battleground state.

An undeterred Trump, who has been holding daily rallies around the country for Republican candidates, filed an emergency request with the US Supreme ​Court on Monday to temporarily block California from counting mail-in ballots from more than 20,000 registered voters who federal officials allege are likely non-US citizens.

California said the lawsuit could disenfranchise 20,000 voters based on vague accusations and that ​the administration's process for identifying noncitizens was flawed and prone to error.

The president, who continues to falsely claim that his loss to Joe Biden in 2020 was caused by widespread ⁠fraud, was due to deliver remarks at 2 pm ET (1900 GMT) at the belated reopening of Washington's Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool. "They call it the House of Satan."

Michigan Democrat Abdul El-Sayed’s Senate campaign said it raised $2.4 million on Sunday after his former primary opponent, US Representative Haley Stevens, withdrew her endorsement and publicly backed Republican Mike Rogers https://t.co/BV9UNqGha5

— Bloomberg (@business) November 2, 2026

Nonpartisan analysts generally favour Democrats' chances ​of winning a majority in the House of Representatives. Winning control of the Senate will be trickier, with those analysts now seeing races in traditionally Republican-leaning states including Texas, Kansas and Iowa as competitive for the opposition party, giving it more options for a path to the majority.

Control of either chamber would constrain Trump's ability to pass legislation and empower Democrats to investigate his administration, while a Senate majority would also allow them to block his appointees to federal courts, including the Supreme Court.

Michigan rift

Stevens called on El-Sayed to condemn an outside group's ad that she said blames Israel for high grocery prices.

El-Sayed rejected Stevens' demand, saying she ‌was creating ⁠a distraction by revisiting a primary election she lost months prior.

"You guys love to play the condemn game," he told reporters on Saturday when asked about Stevens' demand. "I've already been clear that that ad was not made by me, and I do not agree with the contents of that ad."

"He's lied about his relationships with the Muslim Brotherhood, a terrorist organization that's banned in eight Muslim countries."

"She's really reached a point where she felt like her constituents, the people that she cares about, and the people she knows and loves are scared and frightened by some rhetoric that's coming out," Marcotte said ​in an interview with Reuters from the porch of her home in Birmingham, a northern Detroit suburb.

Democratic Congresswoman Haley Stevens is heckled while appearing alongside Republican Mike Rogers, whom she has endorsed in the Michigan Senate race.

— Middle East Eye (@MiddleEastEye) November 2, 2026

The Trump administration's attempt to intervene in Alaska's Senate race faltered when a federal judge dismissed the US Justice Department's lawsuit on Sunday that sought to block certification of the results if Republican incumbent Senator Dan Sullivan narrowly loses.

The Justice Department argued voters may be confused by the presence of a challenger named Daniel Sullivan Jr on the same ballot.

The issue has roiled the campaign over the last several days after the New York Times reported that Democrat Mary Peltola's campaign was involved ⁠in recruiting the latter ​Sullivan into the race as a spoiler.

Peltola has denied involvement, and Sullivan Jr has denied coordinating with Peltola's campaign.

El-Sayed has called questions about his loyalty to the US "shameful".

The verbal attacks fit a broader pattern of inflammatory rhetoric from some Republicans targeting Arab Americans, Muslims and transgender people and portraying Democrats as communists and dangerous radicals ahead of the midterms.

Stevens' mother, Maria Marcotte, said her daughter decided to endorse Rogers because of what she described as dangerous political ⁠rhetoric from El-Sayed, pointing in part to his past appearances with Hasan Piker, a left-wing streamer who has been criticised for his comments about Israel and American Jews.

"She's really reached a point where she felt like her constituents, the people that she cares about, and the people she knows and loves are scared and frightened by some rhetoric that's coming out," Marcotte said in an interview with Reuters from the porch of her home in Birmingham, a northern Detroit suburb.
Democratic voter Pamela Johnson, 72, criticised Stevens after casting her ballot for El-Sayed in Warren, a Detroit suburb: "Haley Stevens ⁠is a traitor."
Alaska intervention falters

The Trump administration's attempt to intervene in Alaska's Senate race faltered when a federal judge dismissed the US Justice Department's lawsuit on Sunday that sought to block certification of the results if Republican incumbent Senator Dan Sullivan narrowly loses.
The Justice Department argued voters may be confused by the presence of a challenger named Daniel Sullivan Jr on the same ballot.

The issue has roiled the campaign over the last several days after the New York Times reported that Democrat Mary Peltola's campaign was involved ⁠in recruiting the latter Sullivan into the race as a spoiler.
The senator said on Sunday he would accept the results of Tuesday's election even as the Trump administration presses a criminal investigation into the issue.
Peltola has denied involvement, and Sullivan Jr has denied coordinating with Peltola's campaign.

"I think it's great that it got thrown out," said Aileena Bird, a 24-year-old resident of Wasilla, Alaska, who said she voted for Peltola. "I think that more should be done to fight against what Trump has been doing in trying to suppress the voters."

headline: Solano targets SAFF Cup semi-finals
description: Pakistan’s head coach backs team ahead of India clash
author: Sports Desk
article_text:
With a high-stakes clash against arch-rivals India looming, Pakistan football team head coach Nolberto Solano has urged his side to challenge the occasion at the SAFF Championship 2026, declaring that every match will be treated as a final as the Green-shirts target a place in the semi-finals.

Confident in his players' abilities, Solano has called for unity, discipline and defensive solidity, insisting that Pakistan have what it takes to compete despite the absence of overseas-based players.

Speaking at a press conference at a local hotel in Islamabad on Monday evening, Solano acknowledged that every opponent would pose a tough challenge but said Pakistan were determined and confident heading into the competition.

“Every match is always tough, as usual, and we are looking forward to the challenge. We are trying to build a strong team and I believe we are not far from achieving our goals. We have already achieved success in the Maldives, so we understand the level of competition. We have also played in Indonesia. We know what we need to do,” he said.

Pakistan will face India and the Maldives in the group stage, with Solano identifying qualification for the semi-finals as the team's primary objective.

“We will take things step by step. Thursday’s match against India is a big one, followed by the game against the Maldives. Our focus is on these two matches so that we can qualify for the semi-finals. We have to treat every match as a final. The first final will be against India and the second against the Maldives,” he said.

Discussing the significance of the Pakistan-India rivalry, Solano compared it to the football rivalry between his home country, Peru, and Chile.

“The rivalry between Peru and Chile is similar to that between Pakistan and India. It carries the same intensity. I understand very well how important these matches are for the fans. We want to make people happy because we know what these games mean to them,” he said.

The former Peru international also emphasised that football was a team sport and that success required every player to contribute collectively.

“We have to play as a united team. Football is not about one individual; it is a collective game. Whether we are attacking or defending, we have to perform as a team,” he added.

Pakistan will be without its overseas-based players during the initial stage of the competition, as the championship is not being held during a FIFA international window. However, Solano insisted that their absence would not be used as an excuse and expressed full confidence in the abilities of local players.

“At the start of this competition, we cannot include our diaspora players because it is not being held during a FIFA window. However, we are giving local players an opportunity and assessing the talent available here. There are no excuses. We believe in our players,” he said.

He further stated that the national team's doors remained open to every player with the required ability and the right mentality.

“We are gradually expanding our talent pool. Any player with the ability and the right attitude has a chance to represent the national team,” he added.

“We first try to become a solid team. Our strategy is to avoid conceding goals because some of our strongest players belong to the defensive department,” he said.

Solano also highlighted the importance of a strong domestic football structure.

“We have to look ahead. We have talent, but these young players need support. They need a strong structure and clubs. The situation was similar in my country, Peru. Gradually, young players continued to improve and their abilities developed further,” he said.

Welcoming the announcement of a professional football league in Pakistan next year, Solano described it as an important development for improving players' physical conditioning and the overall standard of the game.

“It is important for this generation of players to become physically fit and cover more ground. It is great news for us that Pakistan will have a professional league next year. Our current players have never had the opportunity to go through a pre-season. Pre-season training is extremely important for a player because it lays the foundation for the entire season. Hopefully, we will have this facility soon as well,” he said.

The head coach further explained that the team's formation would depend on the players available and the nature of the opposition, stressing the need to remain tactically flexible.

Pakistan will launch its SAFF Championship 2026 campaign against traditional rivals India on Thursday, with Solano describing the encounter as the team's first major test. The Green-shirts will then face the Maldives in their second group match, with a positive result crucial to their hopes of reaching the semi-finals.

Pakistan are in Group B with India and Maldives, while Group A comprises Bangladesh, Bhutan and Sri Lanka.

The top two teams from each group will progress to the semi-finals.

Pakistan will face India in their opening match on November 5. India have announced a second-string side for the event. Their senior team will travel to New Zealand for two friendly matches. They will face the hosts in Auckland on November 12 and Christchurch on November 15.

Nepal is missing the event for the first tme in history due to suspension issue.

headline: Shah Rukh Khan turns 61 as Bollywood stars celebrate the 'King' ahead of new film
description: Suhana Khan, Kajol, Kareena Kapoor, Anil Kapoor among others lead tributes as SRK unveils 'King' song 'Tu Mil Jaaye'
author: Life And Style Desk
article_text:
Bollywood superstar Shah Rukh Khan marked his 61st birthday with a special treat for fans, unveiling Tu Mil Jaaye, the first song from his much-awaited film King, as birthday wishes poured in from family, friends and colleagues across the film industry.

From his daughter Suhana Khan sharing a heartfelt tribute to Kajol, Kareena Kapoor Khan, Shilpa Shetty and Anil Kapoor celebrating the actor, the occasion highlighted the affection he continues to command across Bollywood.

The celebrations also extended to Mumbai, where fans gathered outside his residence, Mannat, to mark the birthday of the man fondly known as Bollywood's King Khan.

Screengrab: suhanakhan2, theshilpashetty/Instagram

Shah Rukh's daughter Suhana Khan took to Instagram to celebrate her father, sharing a picture of the poster of his upcoming film King. Keeping her message short and sweet, she wrote, "Happy birthday king."

Shilpa Shetty also shared a loving birthday tribute on her Instagram Story, calling Shah Rukh her forever Baazigar. Sharing a picture with the superstar, she wrote, "To the one and only King Khan. My forever Baazigar, who wins in every heartbeat. Happy birthday, wishing you endless love, laughter, great health and happiness always."

Screengrab: sonamkapoor, kajol/Instagram

Kajol, who shares a much-loved on-screen history with Shah Rukh, also sent him birthday wishes. Sharing a message on her Instagram Story, she wrote, "Happy Birthday SRK! Stay the absolute rockstar that you are. Sending you the biggest hug today!"

Kareena Kapoor Khan also joined the celebrations with a special Instagram post, sharing a glimpse connected to King. Her caption read, "Happy Birthday King. The forever Ruler of the kingdom. Let's dance together... Can't wait. 24-12-26."

Screengrab: karanjohar/Instagram

Taking to X, the actor posted a photograph of the Bandra-Worli Sea Link illuminated with his pictures and birthday wishes.

The actor also marked the occasion by unveiling Tu Mil Jaaye, the first song from King, giving fans an early glimpse of the film's music.

Featuring Shah Rukh Khan and Deepika Padukone, the romantic track is composed by Sachin-Jigar, with vocals by Arijit Singh and Madhubanti Bagchi. British singer Ed Sheeran has also contributed an English rap to the song.

The release offers fans their first musical glimpse into the much-awaited film, which promises a blend of romance and action.

headline: Sadiq pinpoints flaws in Babar's batting
description: Former opener suggests technical adjustments to help Pakistan’s star regain form
author: Alam Zeb Safi
article_text:
KARACHI: Former Pakistan Test opener Sadiq Mohammad has identified several technical flaws in Babar Azam's batting, pointing to his early shot selection, footwork, batting stance and failure to judge deliveries outside off stump as areas requiring attention.

In an interview with The Express Tribune Sadiq, who also played county cricket for Gloucestershire, drew on his own experience of overcoming similar batting difficulties to offer Babar a series of technical suggestions. He believes adjustments to Test captain's stance, footwork and timing could help him rediscover his scoring touch.

Recalling how he overcame his own problems, Sadiq said he had struggled with dismissals in the third-slip, gully and backward-point areas during his county career. He discussed the issue with his elder brother Wazir Mohammad, who watched him bat in the nets at Birmingham and suggested technical adjustments.

Sadiq said the advice worked, as he went on to score a century in his very next innings against Warwickshire.

Identifying Babar's first problem, Sadiq believes the right-hander plays his shots too early, with the bat away from his body and his front left toe.

He also highlighted Babar's batting stance, which he believes makes it difficult for the batsman to judge the width of deliveries outside off stump.

According to Sadiq, Babar's back foot touches the off-stump line when he makes contact with the ball. This, he believes, allows bowlers to exploit the sixth-stump line with away-swinging deliveries, tempting Babar into chasing balls outside off stump.

Sadiq suggested that Babar change his guard from leg stump to fourth-leg stump and move his right back foot towards a position between leg and middle stump as the bowler approaches the umpire. He believes this adjustment would encourage bowlers to target the stumps rather than exploit the space outside off stump.

Another concern, according to Sadiq, is Babar's tendency to play the ball too early instead of allowing it to come closer to his body.

He believes this causes Babar's off-side shots to travel towards gully, third slip and backward point. Making contact around six inches away from his left-foot toe, Sadiq said, changes the bat's position from a closed face to an open face, resulting in sliced shots that travel behind square in the air rather than along the ground.

He also pointed out that Babar does not transfer enough body weight onto his front foot while driving, preventing him from directing the ball towards the front of square.

Sadiq further stressed the importance of watching the ball make contact with the bat, saying Babar's failure to do so is another reason his cover drives travel behind square.

On timing and contact, he advised Babar to make contact with the ball in front of his left front toe while playing on the front foot, keeping his back bent to ensure the ball travels along the ground. He said the same principle should apply when playing off the back foot, with contact aligned with the front-foot toe.

Sadiq believes regular practice in the nets, particularly with the suggested change in stance and foot positioning, could help Babar direct most of his attacking and defensive shots towards the front of square.

Despite identifying these shortcomings, Sadiq expressed confidence in Babar's ability to return to his previous form.

"Babar, in my view, you are still a very good batsman. I suggest you work on my tips, and you will be the same Babar again. For a world-class batsman like you, it should not be difficult to apply these changes in your next outing. Go out and get it right," Sadiq signed off.

Former Pakistan captain Mohammad Yousuf also wrote on X the other day that Babar should be sent to England and Australia to work on his batting flaws.

article_html:
KARACHI: Former Pakistan Test opener Sadiq Mohammad has identified several technical flaws in Babar Azam's batting, pointing to his early shot selection, footwork, batting stance and failure to judge deliveries outside off stump as areas requiring attention.

In an interview with The Express Tribune Sadiq, who also played county cricket for Gloucestershire, drew on his own experience of overcoming similar batting difficulties to offer Babar a series of technical suggestions. He believes adjustments to Test captain's stance, footwork and timing could help him rediscover his scoring touch.

Recalling how he overcame his own problems, Sadiq said he had struggled with dismissals in the third-slip, gully and backward-point areas during his county career. He discussed the issue with his elder brother Wazir Mohammad, who watched him bat in the nets at Birmingham and suggested technical adjustments.

Sadiq said the advice worked, as he went on to score a century in his very next innings against Warwickshire.

Identifying Babar's first problem, Sadiq believes the right-hander plays his shots too early, with the bat away from his body and his front left toe.

He also highlighted Babar's batting stance, which he believes makes it difficult for the batsman to judge the width of deliveries outside off stump.

According to Sadiq, Babar's back foot touches the off-stump line when he makes contact with the ball. This, he believes, allows bowlers to exploit the sixth-stump line with away-swinging deliveries, tempting Babar into chasing balls outside off stump.

Sadiq suggested that Babar change his guard from leg stump to fourth-leg stump and move his right back foot towards a position between leg and middle stump as the bowler approaches the umpire. He believes this adjustment would encourage bowlers to target the stumps rather than exploit the space outside off stump.

Another concern, according to Sadiq, is Babar's tendency to play the ball too early instead of allowing it to come closer to his body.

He believes this causes Babar's off-side shots to travel towards gully, third slip and backward point. Making contact around six inches away from his left-foot toe, Sadiq said, changes the bat's position from a closed face to an open face, resulting in sliced shots that travel behind square in the air rather than along the ground.

He also pointed out that Babar does not transfer enough body weight onto his front foot while driving, preventing him from directing the ball towards the front of square.

Sadiq further stressed the importance of watching the ball make contact with the bat, saying Babar's failure to do so is another reason his cover drives travel behind square.

On timing and contact, he advised Babar to make contact with the ball in front of his left front toe while playing on the front foot, keeping his back bent to ensure the ball travels along the ground. He said the same principle should apply when playing off the back foot, with contact aligned with the front-foot toe.

Sadiq believes regular practice in the nets, particularly with the suggested change in stance and foot positioning, could help Babar direct most of his attacking and defensive shots towards the front of square.

Despite identifying these shortcomings, Sadiq expressed confidence in Babar's ability to return to his previous form.

"Babar, in my view, you are still a very good batsman. I suggest you work on my tips, and you will be the same Babar again. For a world-class batsman like you, it should not be difficult to apply these changes in your next outing. Go out and get it right," Sadiq signed off.

Former Pakistan captain Mohammad Yousuf also wrote on X the other day that Babar should be sent to England and Australia to work on his batting flaws.

Sadiq also appreciated Yousuf saying former batsman’s suggestion is almost right, but he as an opening batsman has different suggestion.

headline: New cyberattack on supermarket fridges sweeps across Europe
description: Attack raises temperatures in refrigerator, freezer units at dozens of stores, forcing supermarkets to discard food
author: Reuters
article_text:
A hacking attack on European supermarkets spread across the continent on Monday, hitting fridges and ​freezers from Sweden to Belgium and forcing stores to throw away food in an incident that echoed a similar attack in France last month.

The attack, which raised temperatures in refrigerator and ‌freezer units at dozens of stores, hit supermarket groups Ahold Delhaize and Colruyt in Belgium and Luxembourg, as well as Swedish grocers ICA and Coop. Furniture-to-meatballs retailer IKEA also saw at least one store affected.

"Everything is destroyed," Engla Ingwall, sales manager at an ICA franchise store in Stockholm, told Reuters during a visit to the store on Monday, adding the attack occurred at 2 am (0100 GMT) but was only noticed hours later.

"There has been a cyberattack and all our freezers reached 50 degrees (Celsius)."

A spokesperson for privately held ICA said the company ​was aware that a "limited number of stores were affected by an incident overnight, which impacted their refrigeration and freezer systems".

The latest incidents follow an attack in France last month when police said hackers seized control of ​cooling units at hundreds of supermarkets, causing fires and food losses. Ahold also reported a cybersecurity incident to police last month.

While no one has claimed responsibility for either attack, ⁠the incidents have heightened concerns among European authorities about hybrid threats to infrastructure amid growing security tensions since Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine.

Moscow has repeatedly denied involvement in sabotage or hybrid warfare operations. Reuters could not establish who was ​behind Monday's attacks or whether they were linked to the incidents in France.

"It is not known who is behind this attack, and it may never be determined," said Katrien Eggers, spokesperson for Belgium's Centre for Cybersecurity, adding she was concerned ​about the growing number of incidents, in part due to AI.

"All IT systems are potentially vulnerable, and AI can now be used to successfully exploit these weaknesses — especially by sophisticated actors," she said.

'Retail is an easy target'

From refrigerators and heating systems to security cameras and alarms, an expanding range of devices once largely mechanical can now be monitored and controlled remotely, creating new opportunities for cybercriminals.

At least some of the refrigerator units affected on Monday used temperature control technology from Danish firm Danfoss that was also targeted in the French ​attack. The firm said it had been working with customers to implement fixes.

The European Commission said the latest incidents highlighted how digital threats are becoming increasingly disruptive.

"They are a deliberate attempt to disrupt our food supply chain and undermine ​consumers' confidence in it – a warning that we must take seriously," said EU commissioner for agriculture Christophe Hansen. "The repeated occurrence of these cyberattacks is deeply concerning."

A spokesperson for Colruyt Group, which operates Spar stores in Belgium under a franchise system, said five shops ‌had their ⁠fridge systems attacked.

In Ireland, wholesaler Musgrave said the incident affected systems in 13 of its SuperValu stores, forcing it to remove some chilled and frozen products from sale.

"Our monitoring systems alerted us to the issue, and we took immediate action," it said in a statement. "Our investigation is ongoing."

Tom Hegel, a researcher at cybersecurity firm SentinelOne, said such attacks were typically linked to extortion, political motives or nation-state operations, with the absence of financial demands in recent cases pointing instead to sabotage.

"Retail is an easy target because retail chains run enormous estates of refrigeration controllers, building management systems, door access panels and point-of-sale gear," he said, adding it was hard to trace hackers targeting such systems.

"An attacker who logs into ​an exposed control panel leaves almost nothing behind ... A teenager ​and an intelligence service would look much the ⁠same from the defender's side."

'It's very scary'

Carrefour, which was badly hit in last month's French attack, said 15 of its 700 stores in Belgium were affected. IKEA said one store in Belgium had been impacted and that it could not rule out disruptions at other locations.

Privately held Swedish grocery chain Coop said that 7 of its 800 stores were ​affected by a cyber incident involving unauthorised tampering with its refrigeration systems. It said Danfoss was among its suppliers.

Luc De Laet, founder and owner of Belgian butchery ​chain De Laet & Van Haver, said ⁠he was woken at 3:30 am by an employee telling him there was a problem. He rushed to his store south of Antwerp and found the fridges turned up as high as 18 C.

He estimated the incident ruined about €15,000 ($16,800) worth of meat.

"It's very scary. They are hacking the system that is doing the registration of the temperature, and they can program it at a distance," he told Reuters, adding that it was infuriating to throw away so much food.

De Laet said he believed ⁠the hackers were ​trying to destabilise European economies. He had contacted police but did not know whether an investigation had been launched.

"I only have two words ​for them: wake up, please, because there's something going on," he said.

headline: 4 polio immunisation workers abducted in K-P’s Tank
description: TTP abducts two others from Azam Warsak, but subsequently lets them go
author: Ramzan Seemab
article_text:
Four polio immunisation workers were abducted by unidentified armed men after being fired upon in Khyber-Paktunkhwa’s Tank district, while two other members of a polio vaccination team, who had been kidnapped in Azam Warsak, were subsequently released.

According to details, the abduction incident in Tank occurred in a village located in the Sheikh Attar union council, where unidentified armed men abducted the four polio vaccination workers.

Police said the gunmen took all the workers to an undisclosed location.

Police have launched an investigation into the incident.

Further details about the identity of the perpetrators and the whereabouts of the kidnapped workers were not immediately available.

In a separate incident, two members of a polio vaccination team were abducted by armed men in the Azam Warsak area of Lower South Waziristan. However, both vaccinators were later released.

Sources said the suspects were affiliated with the proscribed Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan.

The incidents have raised concerns over the security of polio vaccination teams working in the remote region, where they continue to face threats while carrying out the immunisation campaigns.

A day earlier, the National Emergency Operations Centre (NEOC) for Polio Eradication confirmed Pakistan's seventh polio case of the year, reported from K-P. The infected child was a 13-month-old girl belonging to Jan Baz Union Council in Bara tehsil, the NEOC said.

It was the second polio case reported from Khyber district this year.

Of the seven cases reported across the country so far this year, six have emerged from K-P and one from Sindh, according to the NEOC.

headline: PTI's Barrister Salman Safdar meets Imran, Bushra Bibi in Adiala jail
description: The meeting took place for 40 minutes
author: Imran Asghar
article_text:
Barrister Salman Safdar on Monday met Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) founder Imran Khan and his wife Bushra Bibi at Adiala jail.

Imran has been in custody since August 2023, serving a sentence in a £190 million corruption case. He also faces pending trials under the Anti-Terrorism Act in connection with protests on May 9, 2023. He and Bushra Bibi remain incarcerated in Rawalpindi's Adiala jail. They were sentenced on December 20, 2025, to 17 years in prison in the Toshakhana-II case, which pertains to allegations that the couple unlawfully retained a Bulgari jewellery set gifted by the Saudi crown prince during an official visit to Saudi Arabia.

The PTI has been consistently protesting and demanding that the authorities allow Imran's weekly meetings with his friends, relatives and legal team.

In a post on X today, Barrister Safdar said he met the PTI founder and Bushra Bibi for about 40 minutes for a meeting arranged by the jail authorities at 4:30pm.

According to Barrister Safdar, the meeting took place after multiple requests and marked his first meeting with Imran in seven months and with Bushra in 11 months.

“The session was insufficient to cover all cases/legal matters,” the legal counsel lamented in the social media post, adding that the two him of their health and the conditions in which they were being kept in prison.

Safdar added that both had also conveyed fresh instructions regarding certain legal matters and ongoing cases.

The lawyer did not provide further details about the specific legal instructions discussed during the meeting.

The Islamabad High Court (IHC) on September 2 directed the jail authorities to ensure meaningful human interaction, family access, exercise, reading material and other facilities for Imran and his wife, Bushra.

The court held that lawful incarceration did not authorise the avoidable deprivation of human dignity.

In August, the Supreme Court ordered that Imran be shifted to Shifa International Hospital for treatment and directed the government to arrange weekly meetings between him and his family.

On June 18, the IHC had directed Islamabad's advocate general to ensure that a meeting was arranged within seven days between Imran, Bushra and their legal counsel to facilitate the completion of legal formalities and the prosecution of appeals against their conviction in the £190 million reference case.

Barrister Safdar last held a meeting on April 9 with Imran for legal consultation regarding the £190m case.

He stated that Adiala jail authorities had facilitated his meeting in compliance with IHC orders, adding that the meeting lasted 60 minutes.

The SC had previously ordered the formation of a medical team to examine Imran's eye after Barrister Safdar's report quoted the PTI founder as stating that "only 15%" vision remained in his right eye. The court also directed that both the medical examination and telephonic contact with his children be completed before February 16.

article_html:
ISLAMABAD:

Barrister Salman Safdar on Monday met Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) founder Imran Khan and his wife Bushra Bibi at Adiala jail.

Imran has been in custody since August 2023, serving a sentence in a £190 million corruption case. He also faces pending trials under the Anti-Terrorism Act in connection with protests on May 9, 2023. He and Bushra Bibi remain incarcerated in Rawalpindi's Adiala jail. They were sentenced on December 20, 2025, to 17 years in prison in the Toshakhana-II case, which pertains to allegations that the couple unlawfully retained a Bulgari jewellery set gifted by the Saudi crown prince during an official visit to Saudi Arabia.

The PTI has been consistently protesting and demanding that the authorities allow Imran's weekly meetings with his friends, relatives and legal team.

In a post on X today, Barrister Safdar said he met the PTI founder and Bushra Bibi for about 40 minutes for a meeting arranged by the jail authorities at 4:30pm.

Imran Khan’s lawyer, Barrister Salman Safdar, was finally allowed to meet with him in Adiala Jail for 40 minutes after 7 months.

“Today at 4:30 PM, Adiala Jail authorities facilitated a 40-minute meeting with Mr. Imran Khan and his wife, Bushra Imran. After repeated… pic.twitter.com/a2vgIk6fjo

— PTI (@PTIofficial) November 2, 2026

According to Barrister Safdar, the meeting took place after multiple requests and marked his first meeting with Imran in seven months and with Bushra in 11 months.

“The session was insufficient to cover all cases/legal matters,” the legal counsel lamented in the social media post, adding that the two him of their health and the conditions in which they were being kept in prison.

Safdar added that both had also conveyed fresh instructions regarding certain legal matters and ongoing cases.

The lawyer did not provide further details about the specific legal instructions discussed during the meeting.

https://t.co/jAjfJULunS

— PTI (@PTIofficial) November 2, 2026

The Islamabad High Court (IHC) on September 2 directed the jail authorities to ensure meaningful human interaction, family access, exercise, reading material and other facilities for Imran and his wife, Bushra.

The court held that lawful incarceration did not authorise the avoidable deprivation of human dignity.

In August, the Supreme Court ordered that Imran be shifted to Shifa International Hospital for treatment and directed the government to arrange weekly meetings between him and his family.

On June 18, the IHC had directed Islamabad's advocate general to ensure that a meeting was arranged within seven days between Imran, Bushra and their legal counsel to facilitate the completion of legal formalities and the prosecution of appeals against their conviction in the £190 million reference case.

Barrister Safdar last held a meeting on April 9 with Imran for legal consultation regarding the £190m case.

Read: Imran in good health, high spirits: lawyer

He stated that Adiala jail authorities had facilitated his meeting in compliance with IHC orders, adding that the meeting lasted 60 minutes.

The SC had previously ordered the formation of a medical team to examine Imran's eye after Barrister Safdar's report quoted the PTI founder as stating that "only 15%" vision remained in his right eye. The court also directed that both the medical examination and telephonic contact with his children be completed before February 16.

headline: Govt slashes petrol by Rs3.4, high-speed diesel by Rs7.76
description: New petrol price is Rs374.51 while HSD is Rs395.2
author: Zaigham Naqvi
article_text:
The federal government on Monday slashed the price of petrol by Rs3.4 per litre and that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs7.76 for November 3.

A press release from the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority said the new petrol price was Rs374.51 while HSD was Rs395.2.

Earlier today, the government announced that oil refineries would bear a burden of Rs15 billion per month, which would allow petrol to be sold Rs15 cheaper than it was in the global market amid the US-Israeli war on Iran.

On July 17, the government announced a new pricing mechanism under which petroleum product prices would be reviewed and notified daily, replacing the weekly pricing mechanism, as renewed tensions between the United States and Iran continued to drive volatility in global oil markets and raise concerns over fuel supplies.

On September 13, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif announced a special relief scheme offering Rs100 per litre off petrol for motorcycles, three-wheeler rickshaws and cars with engines up to 800cc, in an attempt to shield lower-income consumers from the impact of rising petroleum prices.

Under the proposal, an estimated 11.8 million beneficiaries would be covered. Around 10 million two-wheeler users and 800,000 three-wheeler users would be entitled to relief on 20 litres of fuel per month, translating into a maximum monthly benefit of Rs2,000 per beneficiary.

Another one million users of cars up to 800cc would receive relief on 30 litres per month, providing them with a maximum benefit of Rs3,000 each.

On Sept 17, the government reintroduced austerity and fuel conservation measures amid rising fuel prices, tightening business operating hours and restricting public events.

Under the measures, notified with immediate effect, shops, markets, shopping malls, bazaars, departmental stores, grocery stores, general stores and kiryana shops would close by 9pm throughout the week, according to a notification issued by the Cabinet Division.

Marriage halls, marquees and other commercial venues hosting festive events would close by 10pm, while restaurants, cafes, eateries, food outlets and standalone fruit and vegetable shops would be allowed to operate until 11pm. Takeaway and home delivery services would remain exempt from the timing restrictions.

headline: Trump could launch nuclear strike on Iran within days, claims Tucker Carlson
description: Warns a nuclear explosion at Pickaxe Mountain can contaminate the Gulf, threaten water supply of 100 million people
author: Anadolu Agency
article_text:
US commentator Tucker Carlson claimed on Sunday that the Trump administration could be days away from launching a nuclear strike on Iran, alleging that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu was pressuring President Donald Trump to authorise an attack on a suspected nuclear site in central Iran.

In a lengthy post on X, Carlson identified the potential target as Pickaxe Mountain, where Israeli intelligence allegedly believed Iran had resumed its nuclear enrichment program.

Carlson is a conservative political commentator and former Fox News host whose program, Tucker Carlson Tonight, aired from 2016 to 2023.

He now hosts an independent political show on X, where he regularly comments on US foreign policy and international affairs.

Carlson claimed conventional US weapons could not penetrate the estimated 300 feet of solid granite protecting underground tunnels at the site, leaving a nuclear strike as the only military option.

"Bibi (Netanyahu) calls Trump about it every day," Carlson quoted an unnamed informed observer as saying.

Carlson argued that Netanyahu's political survival was driving his push for further military action. He claimed Netanyahu needs Trump's intervention to secure a 61-seat majority in the Knesset following the latest election results, warning that otherwise he could lose power and face investigations and possible imprisonment.

He also alleged that Netanyahu has been pressing senior US officials, including Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth and US Central Command chief Adm Brad Cooper, to resume major combat operations.

Carlson also claimed that Secretary of State Marco Rubio and CIA Director John Ratcliffe were following Netanyahu's lead.

He further said former president Barack Obama had also opposed the Iran peace agreement being drafted in Doha.

Fears of regional escalation

Carlson said US allies in the Middle East were increasingly concerned about renewed fighting. He claimed Netanyahu secretly travelled to Abu Dhabi on September 27 to persuade the UAE to support a final attack on Iran, but Emirati officials refused.

Warning of the economic consequences, Carlson said eight months of conflict had severely affected Gulf economies, as well as global energy and fertiliser markets. He claimed 11 of the world's approximately 850 oil supertankers were badly damaged in the Strait of Hormuz in October alone.

He also warned that a nuclear explosion at Pickaxe Mountain could contaminate the Gulf and threaten the water supply of around 100 million people.

Carlson argued that a US nuclear strike could establish a dangerous precedent, potentially encouraging Russia to use nuclear weapons against Ukraine, triggering renewed nuclear tensions between India and Pakistan, and prompting North Korea to attack Seoul.

"After the first nuclear strike, World War Three is inevitable. That war would be short and final," he wrote.

He further alleged that the Trump administration had quietly revised US nuclear doctrine since February to make the first use of so-called "battlefield nukes" easier and more likely.

Vance, Witkoff urge Trump to pursue diplomacy

Carlson said Trump could decide by November 7 whether to authorise the use of nuclear weapons, adding that Vice President JD Vance and special envoy Steve Witkoff were urging him to pursue a diplomatic agreement with Tehran.

Although acknowledging that negotiations would be difficult, Carlson said people who had spoken with Iranian decision-makers believed there was a consensus that further conflict would benefit no one and that an agreement was worth pursuing.

He concluded by warning that the consequences of a nuclear strike would extend far beyond Iran, arguing that the international public had been excluded from decisions that could threaten millions of lives.

"Now would be the time for them to speak up," Carlson wrote.

US could strike remaining Iranian nuclear sites 'within 10 minutes'

Carlson's claims follow Trump's remarks to reporters at his Mar-a-Lago estate in Florida on Saturday that one or two Iranian nuclear facilities remained potential targets and that the US could strike them within 10 minutes.

Trump specifically mentioned Pickaxe Mountain, saying he had military plans for the area, but did not indicate that a nuclear strike had been authorised.

"You probably could look at Pickaxe Mountain, you have to take care of that. We can do that all very quickly," he added.

In an October 16 interview with Newsmax, he explicitly ruled out using nuclear weapons against Iran.

Separately, Axios reported that Trump and Netanyahu held a tense phone call on Saturday, citing Israeli and US sources. According to the report, Netanyahu is pushing for renewed military action immediately after Tuesday's US midterm elections, while Trump prefers to allow diplomatic negotiations to continue.

A White House official said the administration does not comment on sensitive military plans, adding that Trump is keeping all options open to prevent Iran from obtaining a nuclear weapon.

Secretary of State Rubio has also said no final decision has been made on resuming strikes.

Iran, meanwhile, denies any nuclear activity at the Pickaxe Mountain complex. Its supreme leader has warned Washington and Tel Aviv against launching further attacks.
